a52.speaker: Harvard University
a52.speech: Expressed concern over and pointed to the adventurist decree prompted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio suspending processing of foreign student visas.

a52.speaker: China
a52.speech: Immediately turned the situation to its advantage by calling on the rejected foreign minds to come flocking to it, where the doors of the universities of Shanghai and Beijing would be open to them.

a155.speaker: Mohamed B. Dembélé, new secretary-general of the Commune II section of the URD
a155.speech: In his investiture speech, placed his mandate under the sign of cohesion and grassroots work: “The URD is an inclusive party, open to all without distinction. We must get our shirts wet in every neighbourhood to make the URD the leading political force in Commune II and beyond,” he declared, calling on his comrades to persevere.

a155.speaker: Mohamed B. Dembélé, new secretary-general of the Commune II section of the URD
a155.speech: Says the key to success lies in the active involvement of members, notably through regular meetings, which he considers “the main activity of a political party”.

a306.speaker: Democracy & Governance Advocacy Group (DGA-Malawi) (open letter/statement, signed by Concerned Malawians in the diaspora and at home, coordinator Kondwani Bell Munthali)
a306.speech: "We, Malawians in the diaspora and within the country, issue this urgent appeal to address the deteriorating state of governance and democracy in Malawi"; said that since 1994 the international community has been instrumental in supporting democratic consolidation but that recent governance failures, corruption and systemic inefficiencies have eroded public trust; said that under President Lazarus Chakwera's administration corruption has become endemic, listing the Zuneth Sattar misprocurement worth $150 million, a fertilizer scandal, dubious contracts, fuel bribery, offshore asset purchases, a compromised judiciary and increased money laundering; cited irresponsible borrowing, increased public debt, luxury spending amid crisis, ill-equipped public hospitals and food shortages affecting over 5 million Malawians; warned that the September 2025 presidential election faces significant credibility challenges and that the National Registration Bureau is deliberately making registration difficult in opposition strongholds; said the police and government's silence on November 2024 attacks by ruling party youth against opposition protesters is alarming; criticised key partners like the UK, USA and EU for remaining silent or offering support amid clear governance failures, citing the IMF Extended Credit Facility, EU budget support and the USA Millennium Challenge Compact; urged the international community to convene a governance crisis meeting, condemn political violence, support free and fair elections, investigate corruption, restore the Anti-Corruption Bureau's independence, redirect aid through independent accountable entities, monitor IMF compliance, end impunity for critics' arrests, demand accountability from President Chakwera, impose travel and financial sanctions on selected individuals and businesses, and make the Financial Intelligence Authority independent; "Malawi is steadily becoming a failed state where criminals are increasingly becoming in full control of state affairs. Malawi's democracy is at a crossroads."

a306.speaker: Afrobarometer (surveys)
a306.speech: Highlight growing dissatisfaction among Malawians, citing concerns over corruption, inequality, hunger, and rising costs of living.

a354.speaker: Government of Ghana
a354.speech: Has announced plans to lease the Komenda Sugar Development Company Limited to West African Agro Limited, an India-based firm, for a renewable term of 15 to 20 years.

a354.speaker: K. T. Hammond, Minister for Trade and Industry of Ghana
a354.speech: Shared this development during a facility visit to the factory in the Central Region; he said the initiative is part of broader efforts to boost the local sugar industry, reduce imports, and create jobs in the region.

a496.speaker: Save the Children (UK charity)
a496.speech: Has warned that at least 95,000 mothers may give birth without a skilled health worker in the next 12 months due to aid cuts ; said on Wednesday that the situation could put thousands of women and newborns at risk of life-threatening complications, particularly in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Yemen and Nigeria ; said the presence of a skilled birth attendant – a trained midwife, doctor or nurse – significantly reduces complications during delivery, improving survival rates for both mother and child.

a496.speaker: United Nations data
a496.speech: Over 700 women and 6,300 newborns died daily from preventable causes related to pregnancy, childbirth and neonatal care in 2023 alone.

a496.speaker: Moazzam Malik, Save the Children UK chief executive
a496.speech: Called on governments to rethink health financing to prevent further disruptions: "Governments must act now to rethink and realign health financing: mobilising domestic resources, taxing harmful products, coordinating donor support and investing in resilient primary health systems. The future of universal health coverage depends on bold decisions today" ; urged World Health Organisation member states to adopt resolutions to strengthen global health financing and bolster the health workforce by 2030.

a516.speaker: A neighbour of the bereaved family (anonymous)
a516.speech: According to testimonies gathered on the spot, this family was targeted for reasons of witchcraft: "It is not the first time, people die accused of being sorcerers but neither the evidence nor the culprits are ever found," a neighbour of the bereaved family said indignantly. He asks that justice be done.

a516.speaker: Jovith Bayavuge, communal administrator (Mugina)
a516.speech: Asks the population to show vigilance in order to avoid the repetition of such crimes: "It is sad that such a horror has been committed in our commune." Five people have been arrested for the investigation.

a580.speaker: Mark Toner, United States Ambassador to Liberia
a580.speech: Said the laptops and accessories are aimed at strengthening the Government of Liberia's efforts to strengthen its tax administration ; Notes that as Liberia prepares to transition from goods and services tax to value-added tax, this gesture will play a pivotal role in improving auditors' operations ; Said the laptops will also play a key role in tax collection and help move the country forward ; "A robust tax system is essential for any nation's development. By improving the LRA's capacity to collect taxes more efficiently, we are boosting revenue and supporting improvements in Liberia's public services–whether in healthcare, education, or infrastructure. However, we need to ensure revenue transparency and accountability so that resources can be effectively utilized for the country's development. Citizens must see the tangible benefits of their taxes. Our shared goal is to see domestic revenue increase from $700 million to $1 billion by 2027"

a580.speaker: Mark Toner, United States Ambassador to Liberia
a580.speech: Says the U.S. Government is proud to support Liberia in this important transition to VAT, and that through the LEAD Activity, America will continue to work closely with the LRA, particularly its Domestic Tax Department, to ensure the successful implementation of VAT, adding "This support will include training and capacity building for staff and field offices, helping to create a more efficient and transparent tax system." ; Continues that the donated equipment will play a key role in improving operational efficiency and accountability and helping build public trust in the Revenue Authority.

a580.speaker: Dorbor Jallah, Commissioner General of the Liberia Revenue Authority
a580.speech: Lauds the U.S. Embassy for the kind gesture ; Highlights the long existing relationship between Liberia and the United States that has helped in strengthening domestic revenue in Liberia ; Notes that support from the U.S. government and other international partners has contributed greatly to extensive growth in the mobilized revenue sector ; Underscores that from the more than US$700 million in the national budget, only US$40 million in resources is from international partners, attributing the improvement of domestic revenue generation to support from the U.S. government and other partners.

a627.speaker: US State Department
a627.speech: Has issued instructions to the agencies implementing PEPFAR (President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief) to resume HIV services immediately, despite the 90 day “pause” in US aid.

a627.speaker: Mozambican parliament's HIV/AIDS Prevention Office
a627.speech: Says this is a “limited exemption”, for the sole purpose of saving lives, under which HIV treatment services can be resumed, including counselling, HIV testing, preventing and treating opportunist infections (including tuberculosis), laboratory services, and management of the medical supply chain ; says the exemption covers tests of HIV viral loads “which allow monitoring of the patient to guarantee that the medicines for treating HIV are effective”, and that the treatment of tuberculosis is covered because “TB is the greatest cause of death among people living with HIV”; the “limited exemption” does not cover “activities that involve abortion or family planning”, or “gender ideology programmes, transgender surgery, or other activities that do not save lives”.

a627.speaker: National AIDS Council (CNCS) (statistics)
a627.speech: The latest statistics available on the HIV epidemic in Mozambique show that 12.5 per cent of adults over 15 years of age are HIV-positive, with higher prevalence among women (15 per cent) than men of the same age, the most affected group being girls and young women aged 15 to 24, among whom 23,000 new infections were registered in 2023, three times higher than among men of the same age; the CNCS believes that, over the past two decades, 1.7 million new HIV infections and 1.1 million HIV-related deaths have been avoided.

a627.speaker: Mozambican parliament's HIV/AIDS Prevention Office
a627.speech: Argues that these results “reflect the positive impact of consistent public policies, of expanding the coverage of the health services, and of mobilising national and international resources”.

a857.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi (financial market updates)
a857.speech: Only showed forex figures up to August, when the country had $549.85 million — just 2.20 months of import cover; thereafter the central bank's financial market updates no longer show the forex position, both official and private sector reserves, preceded by updates that started to combine the official and private sector reserves.

a857.speaker: National Statistical Office of Malawi
a857.speech: Reported recently that total exports for the first half of 2024 amounted to just $257.8 million, reflecting a 20.1 percent decline from $322.5 million during the same period in 2023.

a857.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a857.speech: In August, expressed concern over the issue and urged the authorities to work on the crisis by making necessary fiscal and monetary policy adjustments to sustain the Extended Credit Facility.

a857.speaker: Malawian authorities
a857.speech: Have ruled out currency devaluation several times, citing the devastating impact on low income earners.

a1042.speaker: Coalition of Community Networks and Civil Society Organisations in Nigeria (statement issued in Abuja)
a1042.speech: condemned the proposal contained in the UN80 reform initiative to “sunset” UNAIDS by the end of 2026, describing the move as “ill-timed” and a “betrayal” of millions of people living with and affected by HIV ; “Any attempt to dismantle UNAIDS at this point risks reversing hard-won gains, undermining donor confidence (including from key external partners such as PEPFAR and the Global Fund), and sending a chilling message to communities still grappling with the epidemic.” ; “The proposal to dismantle UNAIDS is not only ill-advised but dangerously shortsighted and a betrayal of communities living with and affected by HIV.” ; “AIDS is not over, and the global AIDS response has been upset in recent times that it requires deliberate and concerted efforts to achieve the SDG target of ending AIDS by 2030.”

a1042.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General (report “Shifting Paradigms: United to Deliver” under the UN80 Initiative, 18 September)
a1042.speech: “We plan to sunset UNAIDS by the end of 2026. This would entail mainstreaming capacity and expertise into relevant entities of the UN development system in 2027.”

a1042.speaker: Coalition of Community Networks and Civil Society Organisations in Nigeria
a1042.speech: noted that UNAIDS is the only UN agency with communities and civil society at the “heart of its mandate and governance,” and that removing this structure would silence the voices of women, young people, and key populations most affected by HIV; warned that UNAIDS has been a lifeline and dismantling it now would cost lives ; “Who will assume the leadership role in coordinating the global HIV response? Has the UN abandoned its commitment to end AIDS by 2030? Won't this proposal undermine the target?”

a1042.speaker: Coalition of Community Networks and Civil Society Organisations in Nigeria
a1042.speech: called on the UN Secretary-General and member states to immediately reject the recommendation to sunset UNAIDS and instead strengthen its mandate ; “We acknowledge the importance of reforming and modernising the UN system. However, we reject any attempt to use the UN80 process as a vehicle to dismantle progress in the HIV response.” ; “We stand ready to engage with the UN and Member States to co-create solutions that preserve UNAIDS' legacy and ensure no one is left behind.”

a1238.speaker: Kingdom of Morocco
a1238.speech: welcomes the progress achieved towards the halting of hostilities and attacks against civilians, which began on 7 October 2023, two days before the entry into force of the ceasefire agreement in Gaza.

a1238.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad of Morocco (communiqué)
a1238.speech: states “The Kingdom calls on all Palestinian and Israeli parties to give peace a chance and to demonstrate sincere and constructive commitment, far from any circumstantial or opportunistic considerations” ; adds that the Kingdom expresses the wish that this ceasefire agreement be fully respected, and that it allow the halting of attacks against civilians, the return of the displaced and the smooth access of humanitarian aid in sufficient quantities ; continues that the ceasefire agreement should open the way to a real peace process, allowing the establishment of a Palestinian State within the 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital, living side by side and in peace with Israel.

a1238.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco, President of the Al Quds Committee
a1238.speech: emphasised, notably in His Royal Message to the last Arab Summit, that it is fundamental to avoid emerging from one crisis to enter another.

a1253.speaker: Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency (ZIMSTAT) data
a1253.speech: Data provided by ZIMSTAT has shown that Zimbabwe’s diesel imports dipped to a 31-month low of US$57,5 million in August from US$78,3 million in July, due to foreign currency shortages; petrol imports also fell to a 30-month low of US$24 million in July, before recovering marginally to US$26 million in August.

a1734.speaker: Elsbeth Akkerman, Ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to Mozambique
a1734.speech: Stated that "the Dutch Government's development strategy is based on the following pillars: Sustainable Development, Gender Equality, Youth Support, Food Security, Water and Climate and all of them are clearly aligned with the development strategy of the Government of Mozambique".

a1734.speaker: Mike Marchington, Director of Finance & Planning, Gorongosa Restoration Project (GRP)
a1734.speech: Stated that "the Program we launched today is yet another affirmation of our commitment to combine conservation and community development. Biodiversity protection, to be successful, must be an inclusive process, with the participation of all, where community participation must result in tangible benefits for them, making communities the greatest guardians of the ecosystem. Finally, we want to state that, as a team, we are committed to the objectives of this program and to the rational use of the resources allocated to the SLDP by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands".

a1734.speaker: Stella da Graça Pinto Zeca, Secretary of State for the Province of Sofala
a1734.speech: Affirmed the Government's commitment to the success of the Program, recognizing that the Program is part of the Government's Plan and the Sustainable Development Objectives of the United Nations that the Government of Mozambique has ratified.

a2050.speaker: Abdi, Somaliland government official
a2050.speech: “We cannot afford to depend on external trade alone. Strengthening domestic revenue collection ensures we can provide essential services and fund critical infrastructure projects,” Abdi said.

a2050.speaker: Somaliland Ministry of Finance (statement)
a2050.speech: Stated that implementation is proceeding as planned, emphasizing collaboration with telecom providers: “Technical integration is complete, and power companies have already enforced the tax. Telecom firms are now fully aligned with the Ministry of Finance’s tax collection system.”

a2050.speaker: Yusuf Mohamed Hussein, economic analyst
a2050.speech: Acknowledged the government’s rationale but warned of potential drawbacks: “This tax will generate significant revenue, enabling Somaliland to invest in development projects and social services. However, for low-income earners, taxing mobile services, electricity, and internet access could make everyday expenses more burdensome.”

a2050.speaker: Mohamed Hussein Warsame, Hargeisa resident
a2050.speech: “This tax is an added burden on those already struggling with high living costs... Internet and mobile services are essential—this move will only make life harder for ordinary citizens.”

a2050.speaker: Layla Ahmed Ismail, Hargeisa resident
a2050.speech: “This tax will help the government reinvest in public services and build infrastructure... If managed effectively, it could benefit all of us in the future.”

a2269.speaker: Fleetwood Haiya, President of the Football Association of Malawi (FAM)
a2269.speech: Has urged Nsanje District Council to ensure that the rehabilitated Nsanje Youth Centre is maintained and developed further for its longevity and continuous use for elite competitions: "As we are handing over the facility, we plead with Council to ensure that it is maintained and developed further. The plan we did is comprehensive for a fully fledged stadium and the agreement was that Council will continue to upgrade the facility up until it is a full stadium." ; "To the people of Nsanje, this is your facility — let us protect it. Let us safeguard it. Most facilities in the country are in bad shape because they were vandalised immediately after being inaugurated." ; "We do not want to see that happen to this facility."

a2269.speaker: Fleetwood Haiya, President of the Football Association of Malawi (FAM)
a2269.speech: "Let me applaud the FAM executive committee for ensuring we completed the facility. As you are aware this project could have been completed in 2023 before actually coming into office but we made a bold decision to ensure it is completed." ; "Our belief is that football should start from the lower level — we need to start the beautiful game in the zones and district before we talk of the national level." ; "The facility is going to foster and realise our dream in making sure that the coaches should identify talent in the area."

a2269.speaker: Mike Kafalaji, Nsanje District Council official
a2269.speech: Assured that they "will make sure to the facility is maintained and as council will use the budget that they have submitted to continue upgrading starting with the constructing of stands".

a2269.speaker: Kinnah Phiri, deputy director of sports in the Ministry of Youth and Sports
a2269.speech: Hailed FIFA and FAM for handing over the facility: "It's a very beautiful facility and we have seen the talent." ; "If people from Nsanje should come together and form a strong team, they will benefit a lot from the facility."

a2302.speaker: Mozambican government and the United States Embassy
a2302.speech: on Monday, in Maputo, presented the 537 million dollar financing agreement under the second Compact of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC); the money comes from the United States of America and will be used for the construction of climate-resilient infrastructure, coastal development and the strengthening of the local economies of Zambezia province that depend on agriculture and fisheries.

a2338.speaker: Ervin Massinga, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a2338.speech: "We are ready to assist whenever the government and armed groups in the Amhara and Oromia regions are ready to hold constructive peaceful dialogue at any place and at any time" ; called on parties engaged in conflict in Amhara, Oromia and other areas of the country to protect civilians, respect human rights and be ready for peaceful negotiation ; said criminal acts and abductions have multiplied amid the conflict in Amhara and Oromia and have created obstacles to the peaceful movement of people, to economic growth and to aid distribution.

a2338.speaker: Ervin Massinga, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a2338.speech: In a statement issued on Monday titled "A message to the people of Ethiopia": "I am proud of the 120-year relationship between the two countries, which has endured through hardship and triumph" ; said the peace council begun in the Amhara region had been a good start and that the Pretoria Agreement needs to be fully implemented so the Ethiopian people can reap the dividends of peace ; "That the political leaders of the Tigray region focus on the interests of the people is a hope shared by many Tigrayans" ; "Entities outside Ethiopia that spread divisive and toxic rhetoric should stop."

a2338.speaker: Ervin Massinga, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a2338.speech: Recalled that he had held formal and informal discussions concerning the national dialogue and the national rehabilitation process, and announced that the United States has provided $16 million in support for rehabilitation and for the operations of the National Rehabilitation Commission.

a2338.speaker: Ervin Massinga, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a2338.speech: Said the humanitarian crisis has increased significantly, detailing that children are out of school, health service delivery is restricted and farmers have been unable to plant crops ; said there is resource exploitation, particularly illegal mining and deforestation, which exacerbates the war and damages the natural environment ; said eight aid workers were killed in 2024, six of those killings taking place in the Amhara region.

a2338.speaker: Ervin Massinga, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a2338.speech: Said all stakeholders have a responsibility to ensure that civic space is protected and that the media are able to work freely.

a2338.speaker: Ervin Massinga, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a2338.speech: Noted that US private companies are playing a key role by participating in investment in Ethiopia, recalling as an example the purchase of 87 Boeing aircraft concluded between Boeing and Ethiopian Airlines in the past year ; noted that the Ethiopian government has been working jointly with international friends, particularly the IMF and the World Bank, for the success of the macroeconomic reform ; said work has been done to link Ethiopian universities with American universities to help raise the quality of education in Ethiopia.

a2338.speaker: Ervin Massinga, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a2338.speech: Said US investment in the health sector has reduced deaths from TB and related diseases, expanded women's pre- and post-natal health services and worked to protect more than 2.1 million citizens from malaria, and that prevention and control work in Ethiopia's health sector will continue extensively, particularly through the Global Health Security program ; added that over the past two decades four billion birr was invested in the health sector through USAID and three billion dollars through the US presidential program known as PEPFAR ; explained that in 2024 $150 million was provided for humanitarian services for refugees and host communities, including internally displaced people, in Ethiopia, which hosts the largest number of refugees in the region ; said the US government is providing $676 million this year for citizens affected by conflict, drought and food shortages, and that $114 million was allocated for the safety net program and $48 million of USAID's $251 million programs for an emergency disaster project.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabiré, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: In extenso address on the state of the nation delivered on Thursday 16 May 2019: recalled that on 18 February the National Assembly received him for his General Policy Statement and granted him its confidence for the conduct of government action, and said he was appearing again to set out the State of the Nation in accordance with Article 109 of the constitution, so that deputies would be aware of the gains of government action, the challenges to be met and the prospects for implementing public policies. Said government action aims to carry out the programme of the President of Faso, His Excellency Mr Roch Marc Christian Kabore, whose vision is "To build, with the people, a Burkina Faso of democracy, of economic and social progress, of freedom and of justice," a programme translated into the National Economic and Social Development Plan (PNDES).

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: Said government action in 2018 was conducted by his predecessor Mr Paul Kaba Thieba, whose patriotic commitment he saluted, in a particularly difficult national context in which the security of property and persons was severely tested; said the country experienced numerous terrorist attacks causing several victims, plus recurrent hostage-takings of national and foreign figures, "barbaric acts which I condemn forcefully"; said terrorism had implemented a divide-and-rule strategy through ethnic community conflicts and targeted attacks on religious buildings and gatherings, a project to destabilise the country by provoking chaos, adding "we are not going to give up or close our eyes." Saluted the memory of all those who fell as victims of terrorism and community clashes and expressed admiration for, and encouragement to, the agents of the devolved administration and local authorities who remained at their posts to ensure the continuity of public service and the presence of the State in difficult areas.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: Said 2018 was also marked by numerous social disturbances which affected the effectiveness of public action; said he understood the impatience of workers, especially in the public sector, because in Burkina Faso's history the State has made commitments that suffered in their implementation, creating a climate of mistrust and sometimes defiance towards authority; said the government, on the instructions of the President of Faso, remained constant in favouring consultation and negotiation. Said he measures the scale of expectations and wished to reassure everyone that the government's aim is to preserve social peace by repairing often serious injustices between workers with the same level of qualification, sometimes within the same corps. Reiterated the Head of State's call for a social truce, launched on 31 December 2018, to create a climate of serenity favourable to the implementation of reforms, and solemnly invited all components of society to unity so that, beyond legitimate differences, the common objective of Burkina Faso's prosperity may be achieved.

a2377.speaker: Roch Marc Christian Kabore, President of Faso
a2377.speech: In his Address to the Nation of 31 December 2017, announced that the government would undertake a reform of the remuneration system, in consultation with the social partners and the other components of the Nation, to give rise to a modern, dynamic civil service oriented towards development and at the exclusive service of users of the public service; also launched a call for a social truce on 31 December 2018.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: Said that despite the adversities the government had not failed in its essential missions: 1) preserving the integrity of the territory and national unity; and 2) ensuring the country's progress on the path of consolidating the fundamental values of freedom, democracy, justice and human rights; and said the difficult context had not hindered wealth creation aimed at improving Burkinabe living conditions. Said he would insist on three essential points: 1) reforming institutions and modernising the administration; 2) developing human capital; and 3) energising the sectors that drive the economy and jobs; noting his intention was not to present a detailed record but to highlight the most salient aspects, with details contained in the annex document transmitted to deputies.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On security: said terrorism, which appeared a few years ago as a threat at the borders, is today a brutal and cruel reality spreading its web throughout the country; said terrorist strikes changed priorities without abandoning objectives, that the government had to reinforce the operational and organisational capacities of the national armed forces and internal security forces and intensify territorial security operations, in which the armed forces neutralised terrorist groups and arrested numerous suspects during large-scale sweep operations in crime-prone areas; paid vibrant tribute to the armed forces and internal security forces for the difficult combat they wage against barbarity. Recalled, against critics, that the forces operate within a framework governed by law and that the country respects and intends to respect all human rights conventions it has signed; said Burkina Faso had proved its legendary hospitality by receiving tens of thousands of refugees, and today hosts more than 25,000 refugees, nearly 5,000 asylum seekers and about 150,000 internally displaced persons, all treated in accordance with international conventions. Said the government would continue efforts to equip units of the armed and paramilitary forces with strategic and specific means, ensure their training, increase numbers and reinforce and pool information systems through partnership with sub-regional and friendly countries outside Africa.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On foreign policy: said Burkina Faso intends to pursue its efforts to shine on the international stage by taking an active part in regional and sub-regional integration and forging relations beneficial to the economy; said the President of Faso chose the China of Beijing to forge a win-win partnership and that the Ouagadougou-Beijing axis is promising for national and sub-regional infrastructure; said the fight against terrorism allowed appreciation of the solidity of cooperation with France and the European Union, which support the strategy against violent extremism and help finance development; said the recent state visit of German Chancellor Angela Merkel gave rise to a G5 Sahel summit and constitutes an important step in strengthening cooperation; said the Ouagadougou-Washington axis is being consolidated with Burkina Faso's eligibility in December 2016 for a second Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) Compact and its eligibility in December 2018 for the regional Compact, with feasibility studies nearing completion, attesting to the confidence of American partners; said diplomatic standing is also measured by the capacity to attract financing - in 2018, 88 agreements were signed for 1,176 billion FCFA - and by the election of the President of Faso to head the G5 Sahel.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On governance and justice: welcomed the smooth conduct of the trial of the coup of 16 September 2015, begun on 27 February 2018 and still ongoing, saying any democrat can rejoice at the stage reached since many were sceptical it would be held; said that, respectful of the sacrosanct principle of separation of powers, the government strongly encourages the judiciary to assume its responsibilities so that justice remains an instrument that strengthens national unity and preserves social peace; said the government had consolidated the performance of justice in technical and operational capacity and in geographic and financial accessibility through the judicial assistance fund; said specialised judicial poles against economic and financial offences judged 12 cases and registered 125 files in 2018; said on the Yirgou tragedy that investigations had progressed, with more than 160 people heard and the preliminary inquiry into the terrorist attack that killed the village chief and his companions closed; said the adoption in May 2018 of the penal code is a guarantee of improved sanctions and reinforced respect for human rights, and that efforts were made on prison activities preparing detainees for reintegration, with some detention houses brought up to standard.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On administrative modernisation and anti-corruption: said modernising the public administration aims to improve its functioning, reinforce its effectiveness and the quality of public management and break with routine practices and red tape; said capital importance is given to the digital transition, with the promotion of e-governance, the e-competition recruitment platform, and the virtual one-stop window of the public administration launched in 2018 giving citizens direct online access to information, procedures, forms and services, with more than 500 administrative procedures now listed; said the special review on implementation of ASCE/LC recommendations noted that some fifty audit and investigation reports carried out in 2018 were officially transmitted to him, that all recommendations were addressed to the ministerial departments concerned, and that he had instructed the government to revisit procedures, strengthen internal control and energise disciplinary boards in order to eradicate the scourges undermining the administration; said the government is working to improve ASCE/LC's investigative missions so it can fully play its role as judicial police officer.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On press freedom: said citizens' access to information is an inalienable right in contemporary democracies; said the government intends to promote a plural and professional press, that accessibility to media was increased through the installation of 35 Digital Terrestrial Television broadcasting stations (29 operational), the reinforcement of the technical facilities of National Television and Editions Sidwaya, and a subsidy of 400 million to 96 press companies, plus a credit line of 667 million FCFA opened in a local bank to finance press companies' investments; said the government remains open to discussions to revise laws to remove any shortcomings hampering media activity, while working to ensure information broadcast is fair and transparent so that disinformation and fake news do not harm public order and human dignity.

a2377.speaker: Audrey Azoulay, Director-General of UNESCO (quoted by the Prime Minister)
a2377.speech: "Every State governed by the rule of law, respectful of individual freedoms, in particular the freedoms of opinion, conscience and expression, rests on a free, independent press, sheltered from all censorship and all coercion."

a2377.speaker: Reporters Without Borders (press freedom ranking, cited)
a2377.speech: Ranked Burkina Faso 36th in the world out of 180 countries and 4th in Africa in terms of press freedom, first among French-speaking African countries.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On economic governance: said the economic recovery observed since 2016 strengthened in 2018, with a growth rate of 6.6% against 6.3% in 2017, 5.9% in 2016 and 3.9% in 2015; said that although the progress is modest it reveals a capacity for resilience allowing a fairly stable macroeconomic environment with well-controlled inflation (2% at end-2018), a controlled budget deficit (4.7% of GDP in 2018) and a low debt ratio (38.4% of GDP in 2018); said the public investment rate rose from 8% in 2017 to 10% of GDP in 2018 but stability is needed to reinforce the trend, and that the government will firmly pursue actions carrying growth strong and sustained enough to favour private-sector development and job creation. Cited new steering instruments: law No. 034-2018 of 27 July 2018 on the steering and management of development, law No. 024-2018 of 28 May 2018 on land-use planning and sustainable territorial development, and the national strategy for promoting growth poles with its action plan.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On regional disparities and decentralisation: said the Emergency Programme for the Sahel in Burkina Faso (PUS-BF) executed 154 investment projects worth 111 billion FCFA in socio-economic, governance and security fields, mostly completed in 2018, and that, in application of the National Assembly's recommendation of 12 September 2018 on the security situation, the government is working to extend the programme to the regions affected by violent extremism; said the Local Economies Development Support Programme (PADEL) had invested about 3 billion FCFA in the Sahel region for 797 informal production unit promoters, built socio-economic infrastructure and financed 617 micro-enterprises run by women and young people, and was extended in 2018 to six regions (East, Centre-North, Centre-East, Boucle du Mouhoun, Centre-South and North) and would be deployed in 2019 to the six remaining regions; said decentralisation frameworks were being renewed through the 2040 prospective vision and the national decentralisation policy with its ten-year strategy, which will improve local authorities' access to public-private partnership financing, loans and diaspora financing, broaden the local tax base, and reform public procurement regulations for local authorities; said the government acted on legislation to favour investment financing through the new business climate monitoring mechanism, the creation of the Burkinabe Investment Agency (ABI) in May 2018 replacing API-BF, and the adoption on 30 October 2018 of the new investment code.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On health: said developing human capital as provided by the PNDES is the means to develop the social sectors of education and health into long-term factors of GDP growth; said the government pursued the construction of health infrastructure nationwide, improved health facilities' technical platforms including dialysis units for the Souro Sanou and Tengandogo University Hospitals, brought 270 of 304 health facilities (88.8%) up to Health and Social Promotion Centre (CSPS) standard and transformed 30 CSPS in rural commune capitals into medical centres; said work under way includes transforming 32 further CSPS into medical centres, opening the Ouagadougou Specialised Institute of Traditional Medicine and Integrated Care (98% complete) and completing the Ouagadougou cancer treatment centre (57% executed, with radiotherapy expected operational within 14 months); said access to health services was facilitated by vigorous recruitment, training and deployment of staff to improve the inhabitants-per-doctor ratio towards WHO norms, and that 2019 should see construction start on the new Bobo-Dioulasso University Hospital and the Ouahigouya dialysis unit.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On water, sanitation and housing: said that pursuing the objective of zero water drudgery, the surface water volume was increased in 2018 to 6,143 million cubic metres through 11 new dams and the rehabilitation of 17 others, that the village hydraulics and simplified drinking water supply programme continues through boreholes, that ONEA's water storage capacity was increased by 6,450 cubic metres from 2017 to 2018 and the national drinking water access rate raised to 74% in 2018; said the sanitation rate rose from 18% in 2015 to about 22% in 2018 with an objective of 34% in 2020; said that in housing, 1,712 social and economic dwellings were built in 2018 alongside the diaspora investment programme within the 40,000 housing programme, and that servicing operations in rural communes had begun, with continued work on urban planning documents, the subdivision of 80 rural commune capitals and the clearing of urban land liabilities in line with Parliament's recommendations.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On education and research: said the government pursued the objective of increasing provision at all levels of education while improving quality, in a context marked by social unrest in education and above all insecurity which caused the closure of many schools and the destruction of educational infrastructure and teaching materials in the regions most affected by terrorist attacks, and that measures were taken to regroup examination-class pupils from closed schools for support courses and a special examination; said emphasis was placed on technical and vocational education with the launch of construction of 6 science lycees, 2 technical lycees, 5 vocational lycees and 5 technical and vocational teaching and training centres (CEFTP), and the recruitment and placement in internships of 200 students destined for technical and vocational teaching, 163 of them in Tunisia; said new curricula are being piloted in 6 regions, that higher education is being strengthened through Polytechnic University Centres (CUP) in the regions and a Virtual University with open digital spaces, with the recruitment of one hundred teachers and 89 temporary teaching and research assistants and the construction of 1,000- and 1,500-seat lecture theatres to make the Ouaga II University site functional; said research gains in 2018 included the strengthening of the National Fund for Scientific Research and Innovation which financed 60 research projects, the recruitment of 37 researchers, and preparatory studies for structuring projects such as technology parks in ICT, renewable energy and agri-food technology.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On employment, women's empowerment and social protection: said a major objective is to fight unemployment and underemployment by facilitating access to quality jobs and social protection, reducing social and gender inequalities and promoting women as dynamic actors of development; said the Youth and Women's Economic Empowerment Programme (PAE/JF) and the Burkina Start-up programme launched in 2017 granted loans to about 20,000 micro-projects run by young people and women; said that through the Integrated Programme for Women's Empowerment (PIAF-BF) the government supported the registration of 875 informal women's businesses and provided 500 women's associations with working capital, investment credit and technology, and that between 2016 and 2018 nearly 438,000 women received credit for income-generating activities; said actions for socially vulnerable people included a project supporting vocational training, employment and entrepreneurship for people with disabilities endowed with 220 million FCFA in 2018, the removal of 2,465 children from the street into foster families or vocational training centres, direct subsistence transfers to nearly 82,000 vulnerable households and integrated care for about 4,300 vulnerable households.

a2377.speaker: Roch Marc Christian Kabore, President of Faso
a2377.speech: At the national forum of persons living with a disability on 21 June 2018, committed to setting up public structures to receive and care for children with intellectual and mental disabilities, to making the forum a permanent event and to strengthening implementation of the sectoral policy "Labour, employment and social protection."

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On transport infrastructure: said the government considerably increased public investment to develop resilient, quality infrastructure to drive structural transformation of the economy; said it completed the construction or strengthening of about 591 km of road and urban roadway and continued works on 664 further km, built or maintained about 1,829 km of rural tracks and completed important crossing structures such as the Mouhoun bridge on national road No. 1; said that for road projects in difficulty the government had contacted implementing partners to find appropriate solutions, citing the Kongoussi-Djibo (lot 2), Didyr-Toma-Tougan and Kantchari-Diapaga-Tansarga-Benin border tarring projects; said talks with the sister Republic of Ghana on a rail interconnection between the two countries are well advanced, offering an additional alternative route to the port of Tema; and said that for the Donsin airport construction project the government chose a Public-Private Partnership for its financing.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On energy and ICT: said energy is an indispensable input and that in 2018 electricity coverage improved significantly with the electrification of 287 new rural localities and the commissioning of mini solar photovoltaic plants supplying 14 medical centres with surgical units; said energy-hungry street lamps were replaced with LED lamps for public lighting in large towns and for health centres, schools and literacy centres in rural areas, and that a "solar backups" operation was launched for 6,000 households connected to SONABEL to free up electricity supply for large industry and raise rural access; said supply rose by 50 MW with the completion of the electrical interconnection with Ghana on the Ouagadougou-Bolgatanga axis and that imports from Cote d'Ivoire were maintained at an average of 70 MW, with an expected increase of 57.5 MW in production once the Fada N'gourma thermal plant and a plant ordered to curb peak hot-season demand are completed, alongside continued construction of several solar photovoltaic plants. On ICT, said the ambition is to guarantee citizens, businesses and the administration access to quality electronic communication services, that a national backbone network totalling 891 km had been built by 2018 with a 307 km section connected to submarine cables via Ghana operational since July 2018, that the adoption of the technologically neutral licence in 2018 favoured 4G deployment, that the extension of the national administration IT network (RESINA) covered 57 localities with about 1,500 interconnected public administration sites, and that actions such as the West Africa Regional Communications Infrastructure Project (PRICAO-BF) and a virtual landing point at Bobo-Dioulasso are planned.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On agriculture, livestock and fisheries: said efforts focused on developing hydro-agricultural schemes and promoting agriculture more resilient to climate hazards, with more than 19,000 ha of lowlands, irrigated and market-gardening perimeters developed out of 35,000 expected and about 6,200 ha rehabilitated, and continued support to producers with subsidised improved seeds, fertilisers and other inputs, animal traction equipment and draught animals; said the modern Pouytenga abattoir was completed and that of Kaya was 90% built, the Ouagadougou Dairy Basin development project was launched and animal health improved through prevention and response to priority animal diseases; said the objective of producing at least 25,000 tonnes of fish each year is already achieved thanks to subsidised fingerlings and fish feed, pond construction and stocking of water bodies; said the government is committed to setting up the Central Purchasing Body for agricultural inputs and equipment and must succeed with the tractor and power-tiller assembly unit project, as well as structuring projects including a central purchasing body for veterinary medicines, the Bobo-Dioulasso Dairy Basin, an animal vaccine production unit, the rehabilitation of the Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso modern abattoirs and the construction of modern abattoirs at Fada N'Gourma, Banfora and Ouahigouya.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On industry, mining and crafts: said industry was one of the most dynamic sectors in 2018, with industrial value added up 5.7%; said projects to process cotton locally - the integrated cotton processing unit at Koudougou and the textile industrial park at Bobo-Dioulasso - are at the memorandum of understanding stage with interested private partners, while the takeover and reopening of the former FASO FANI factory at Koudougou is at the reconstruction site preparation stage; said the organic cotton ginning plant at Koudougou is 50% complete and cotton processing industrial complexes are being set up in Ouagadougou, Koudougou and Bobo-Dioulasso; said the government created an Enterprise Restructuring Fund, cumulatively committing 11.2 billion FCFA and financing 20 restructuring plans; said phase II of the Bobo-Dioulasso industrial zone development is more than 50% advanced. On mining, said gold production reached 51.63 tonnes in 2018 against 46.39 tonnes in 2017, a rise of 11.3%, raising its contribution to the State budget from 226 billion FCFA in 2017 to 266.4 billion FCFA in 2018, with the sub-sector's share of GDP moving from 7.9% in 2015 to 11.4% in 2017 and 10.6% in 2018, exceeding the PNDES target of 10.2% for 2020, and direct investment flows reaching 1,462 billion FCFA in 2018 against 1,388 billion in 2016; said 77% of the recommendations of Parliament's inquiry into the sector have already been translated into action, that the National Anti-Gold-Fraud Brigade and ANEEMAS had their capacities strengthened, ANEEMAS opening its first support office at Gaoua in 2018, and that the Local Development Mining Fund became operational. On crafts, cited the successful 2018 SIAO, the provision of 1,000 looms to strengthen women weavers' capacities, support for the formalisation of artisans, flexible financing of 106 artisans for 511 million, and the start of works on phase two of the Bobo-Dioulasso Artisanal Village (VAB).

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On trade, transport, culture, tourism and sport: said the government made the Export Support Fund operational and strengthened assistance to actors for international fairs and trade shows, and reinforced trade control with the Mobile Control Brigade (BMC), whose action in the edible-oil sector identified and closed 44 clandestine units; said progress was made in modernising transport documents, rejuvenating the vehicle fleet and relaunching Air Burkina, with 42,700 modern driving licences issued in 2018 and production capacity to rise from 120,000 to 160,000 in 2019, secure vehicle registration cards and number plates production begun in April with a capacity of 537,000 cards a year, 556 new heavy goods vehicles imported as at 31 December 2018, and support for Air Burkina to add 3 aircraft in 2018 with the aim of regaining its place in West African skies, opening prospects towards Central Africa in 2019 and reaching financial equilibrium by 2020. Said that for cultural and artistic development the government organised the 2018 National Culture Week (SNC) from 24 to 31 March 2018 in Bobo-Dioulasso on the theme "Safeguarding cultural values: issues and challenges," which recorded nearly 600,000 visitors, and provided financial and technical support to 47 cultural operators' projects worth 357 million FCFA and a subsidy of 1 billion FCFA to 9 film production projects; said support of about 472 million FCFA went to 17 tourism operators' projects; cited sporting performances including the national cycling team winning the tours of Togo, Benin, Mali and Guinea and Burkina Faso winning the Zone 3 karate-do tournament with 29 medals including 12 gold, with special mention of Mr Cheick Ahmed Al-Hassan Sanou, known as Iron Biby, world log-lift champion, and offered warm congratulations to all athletes and federations.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: On the environment and green economy: said socio-economic progress was achieved while respecting environmental preservation rules and that the government tackled climate change and environmental degradation through the promotion of the green economy; cited the planting of 4.2 million seedlings and the recovery of 7,600 hectares of degraded land, the development of 750,000 hectares of forest, and the financing through the Environment Intervention Fund of 197 forest management micro-projects and 32 communal integrated development programmes; cited in urban centres the completion of 5 plastic waste treatment and recovery centres at Gaoua, Manga, Dedougou, Dori and Tenkodogo with two equipped with technical materials, the monitoring of 323 environmental and social management plans (PGES), and support to urban communes for 20 hectares of green space and 114 kilometres of alignment plantations; cited the adoption of the national eco-village creation strategy, the start of investments in pilot eco-villages and the identification of 271 further villages to be transformed, and the provision of equipment and inputs worth 1.5 billion FCFA to 300 women's organisations working in non-timber forest product value chains.

a2377.speaker: Christophe Marie Joseph Dabire, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2377.speech: In conclusion: said the gains from implementing the PNDES are undeniable and would certainly have been better had the security context and social agitation not weighed on these otherwise satisfactory results; said the results were achieved thanks to the commitment of a people determined to fight adversity and unite its energies around the vision of building a Burkina Faso of progress and justice under the leadership of the President of Faso; said he is aware that many challenges remain and the means to meet them are limited, but hope is permitted and "it is together, united and reconciled with ourselves, that we will build a new Burkina Faso," adding that the political dialogue initiated by the President of Faso and his Call for National Reconciliation respond to that imperative. Said that in view of the record presented, the finding is established that despite all destabilisation attempts, Burkina Faso remains standing, and that this strengthens his determination and that of his government to pursue the fight for the economic and social prosperity of the people with the constant support of friendly countries and technical and financial partners, whom he saluted and thanked. Called on all Burkinabe to redouble vigilance and hard work to overcome all adversity, since in 100 years of the homeland's existence the people has always shown courage and unity in sweat and blood; and thanked deputies for their sustained attention, saying he remained at their disposal for any contributions to improving his government's action.

a2513.speaker: Tom Fletcher, UN Deputy Secretary General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator
a2513.speech: "For countries affected by conflict, climate change and economic shocks, a sharp reduction in funding does not mean that humanitarian needs will disappear. Today's allocation of emergency fund funds allows us to quickly direct resources to where they are most needed."

a2554.speaker: Matthias Fechter, operations manager of Acacia Composites
a2554.speech: Explained that construction of the factory began in March 2023, that the machines were imported in June of last year and landed in Namibia two months later, in August 2023: “Between 60 and 70 percent of our super-green products are exported to Germany, and we expect to export 20 percent to South Africa.”

a2554.speaker: Matthias Fechter, operations manager of Acacia Composites
a2554.speech: According to Fechter, his products are of sustainable value and resistant to rot, fading, staining, decay and insect infestation: “The products are excellently suited for outdoor use, are easy to install, maintain and clean.”

a2554.speaker: Heinrich Unland, company director of Acacia Composites
a2554.speech: Said the main goal was to export their products to the entire SADC region as well as to other European countries: “Our products are of the highest quality, and quality is what keeps you in business” ; asked why Acacia Composites chose Namibia for its factory, said: “Our products are cheaper than in Germany. They are somewhat more expensive than those from China, but the quality is high” ; according to Unland, samples of the products have already been sent to a laboratory in Germany for examination and quality testing.

a2554.speaker: Heinrich Unland, company director of Acacia Composites
a2554.speech: According to Unland, more workers will be hired in future because the factory is to run 24/7, with two shifts keeping operations going seven days a week: “If Namibia Breweries can do it, so can we.”

a2554.speaker: Rocketreach (internet platform)
a2554.speech: According to the internet platform “Rocketreach”, Unland is an experienced force in the field of renewable energies, risk management, biomass and much more, lives in Hamburg and is managing director and owner of Apos GmbH.

a2554.speaker: Apos GmbH (company website)
a2554.speech: Offers on its website “solutions for many industries with a focus on board production, pulp & paper, flooring, panels, glue and biomass combined heat and power plants”.

a2677.speaker: Dr. Fidelis Mwazi, Chief Executive Officer of the Namibian Agronomic Board (NAB)
a2677.speech: Outlined the NAB's five-year plan, emphasising its alignment with the recently launched sixth National Development Plan (NDP 6) by President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah ; noted that while Namibia has achieved 100% production in certain food categories, there are limitations in others.

a2677.speaker: Ruth Masake, Deputy Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform
a2677.speech: Encouraged farmers to voice their challenges, emphasising that such meetings are crucial for informing the ministry on how to best support the agricultural sector.

a2744.speaker: Inibehe Effiong, human rights lawyer
a2744.speech: Described as embarrassing the Senate's decision barring Kogi Central Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan from resuming legislative duties despite completing her six-month suspension: “I find the letter of the Senate embarrassing. I find it scandalous. I find it contentious. And I find it very disparaging of the sensibility of the Nigerian people because it is simple,” he said on Channels Television's ‘Politics Today.’ ; Faulted anchoring the Senate's decision on a pending case at the Court of Appeal, saying the pending appeal could not serve as a basis to stop her from resuming after serving the punishment: “Having now served for six months, the issue of suspension has elapsed by operation of law. Suspension no longer exists because it is a definite appeal.” ; Criticised the Senate, noting that its actions towards Mrs Akpoti-Uduaghan would turn the country into a laughing stock in the global community; stressed that it was unfair for her constituency to suffer for six months simply because she refused to change seats, and that there was “no law in support of it”; advised the Senate to recall her immediately.

a2744.speaker: Inibehe Effiong, human rights lawyer
a2744.speech: Pointed out that the saga between Mrs Akpoti-Uduaghan and Senate President Godswill Akpabio was driven by personal ego, evident in the lawlessness of the Senate, and accused Mr Akpabio of using his office to pursue a “personal vendetta”: “It now calls into question whether really there was a modicum of veracity in what Natasha said” ; “This is a personal matter. Nigeria should stop making it about the legislative institution. This is a personal grievance between Senator Akpabio, who is the Senate President, and Senator Natasha. He is now using his office to achieve his own agenda.” He advised the Senate President to allow time and history to vindicate him.

a2744.speaker: National Assembly (letter of 4 August)
a2744.speech: Wrote a letter to Mrs Akpoti-Uduaghan insisting that she could not yet resume legislative activities despite the expiration of her six-month suspension from the Senate.

a2744.speaker: Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)
a2744.speech: Asked Mrs Akpoti-Uduaghan to disregard any attempt by the management of the National Assembly to prevent her from resuming legislative duties, having already served her suspension period; condemned the National Assembly's position, describing it as an attack on women's rights.

a2744.speaker: Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, Senator for Kogi Central
a2744.speech: Accused Mr Akpabio of sexual harassment; alleged at various fora that she was targeted as part of alleged sexual harassment she faced from Mr Akpabio, and on 11 March reported her suspension and alleged sexual harassment by the Senate President to the Inter-Parliamentary Union during its meeting in the United States; on 12 July notified the management of the National Assembly of her intention to resume legislative duties based on the judgement.

a2744.speaker: Binta Nyako, Judge of the Federal High Court in Abuja (judgement)
a2744.speech: The court held that suspending an elected senator for six months was not only disproportionate but also effectively silenced an entire senatorial district for most of the legislative year; the judge toned down her order, framing it like an advisory that left the Senate with the discretion to recall or not to recall her.

a2744.speaker: National Assembly management
a2744.speech: On 13 July maintained that the judgement by the Federal High Court was merely advisory, not an enforceable order.

a2744.speaker: The Senate
a2744.speech: Said that it could not reinstate her.

a3098.speaker: Alassane Amadou Sani, Director of the Legal Documentation and Information Centre (CDIJ)
a3098.speech: For Alassane Amadou Sani, this jewel comes to fill an expectation of the Beninese public and must be a dynamic, structured documentation centre able to host many works, activities and conferences and to contribute to a better dissemination of judicial information in Benin.

a3098.speaker: Marie Elise Gbèdo, Minister of Justice of Benin (Keeper of the Seals)
a3098.speech: According to the Minister of Justice, the centre constitutes a space for the mixing of intellectual knowledge and must be efficient and well organised in order to be a factor of development and growth; the Keeper of the Seals made a commitment, in the name of the government, to play her part fully in the promotion and influence of this legal documentation and information centre.

a3098.speaker: James Knight, US Ambassador to Benin, and Samuel Batcho, national coordinator of MCA-Benin
a3098.speech: Invited the government to support this centre by providing it with human, documentary and financial resources in order to make it a national and even regional reference.

a3104.speaker: Chief of Defence Staff of Nigeria
a3104.speech: Complained of being denied a visa to visit Canada to watch the Invictus games.

a3104.speaker: Nuhu Ribadu, National Security Adviser of Nigeria
a3104.speech: Publicly declared in anger, “to hell with Canada!”

a3104.speaker: Statistician-General / Director-General of the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS)
a3104.speech: Explained on television that the Consumer Price Index (CPI) declined to 24.48 per cent year-on-year in January, adding that this does not mean prices have declined from the previous rate of 34.80 per cent; it simply means the numbers have been rebased from 2009 to 2024. He told viewers that all countries regularly rebase their economies by updating the reference year used to gauge price levels and by changing the basket of goods and services used to measure inflation, to better reflect current consumer spending patterns and ensure the inflation data accurately reflects the economy’s current state.

a3104.speaker: Scott Perry, American congressman
a3104.speech: Announcement that USAID has been sponsoring terrorist organisations, including Boko Haram in Nigeria.

a3104.speaker: Senator Mohammed Ali Monguno, Senate Chief Whip
a3104.speech: Raised a point of order, drawing attention to what he described as Senator Akpoti-Uduaghan’s “improper sitting position.”

a3104.speaker: Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, representing Kogi Central Senatorial District
a3104.speech: Protested the relocation of her seat without prior notice, demanding explanations for the sudden change of her seat, accusing Akpabio of deliberate silencing of her voice and asserting her right to fully represent her people.

a3104.speaker: Senator Godswill Akpabio, Senate President
a3104.speech: Became furious and ordered the Sergeant-At-Arms to take Natasha out of the chamber.

a3104.speaker: General Ibrahim Babangida, former military president of Nigeria (memoir “A Journey in Service”)
a3104.speech: Said he was in Katsina when the annulment of the 12 June 1993 election, won by MKO Abiola of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), was announced by the press secretary of his second-in-command without his knowledge or permission ; said Abacha had become a major force in a “factionalised” military and it was difficult to remove him when he stepped down from power ; admitted that Arthur Nzeribe, who led the Association for Better Nigeria (ABN), was close to him, but denied supporting the activities of ABN.

a3315.speaker: UN high-level officials (Leonardo Santos Simão, SRSG and Head of UNOWAS; Abdou Abarry, SRSG for UNOCA; Mohamed M. Fall, UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator for Nigeria)
a3315.speech: Highlighted the steady progress made in Bama to include joint Government, UN and partners efforts to provide internally displaced persons (IDPs) with humanitarian assistance and livelihood support and initiatives enhancing social cohesion and reintegration through social and economic activities ; also noted the challenges that remain including violence, the threat posed by the climate crisis, and inadequate basic services.

a3315.speaker: UN high-level official (quote unattributed in the article text; visiting SRSG)
a3315.speech: “I returned to Bama today, eight years since my last visit – which was a few months after it was liberated from the insurgency. A lot has changed since then, with marked improvement in the lives of people affected by the crisis. While there is still work to be done to address insecurity and its impact on civilians, I thank the Borno State authorities, donors, UN agencies and partners for their commitment and dedication through this journey that has made Bama what it is today.”

a3372.speaker: Ministry of Agriculture (Malawi)
a3372.speech: Has projected that the country could produce at least 250 000 metric tonnes of maize per cycle from 50 000 hectares that will be committed to irrigation to enhance food security.

a3372.speaker: Benedicto Chambo, Deputy Minister of Agriculture of Malawi
a3372.speech: Said government aims to improve food security by producing maize in three cycles from 50 000 hectares nationwide which will realise at least 750 000MT annually, and that government will support the farmers with farm inputs loans through the National Economic Empowerment Fund (Neef): “The 50 000 hectares is what government is supporting but there are also other farmers who are doing irrigation farming on their own, there are also mega farms where irrigation farming is taking place. We want Malawi to be able to produce more and be able to export. We have been relying on rain-fed but now we want to rely on irrigation so that Malawi should be food secure but also be exporting more.” ; called on farmers at the irrigation scheme and other schemes supported by government to be actively involved, saying with irrigation farming the country is on the right path to stop importing maize.

a3372.speaker: Pilirani Phiri, Dowa Dambo Water Users Association chairperson
a3372.speech: Said the farmers are ready to utilise the whole 400 hectares under the Dowa Dambo Scheme, and that households have had challenges with rain-fed agriculture hence the irrigation scheme is a big relief to them: “Farmers have demonstrated ownership of the project and went to the point of contributing money to buy fuel for tractors so that tilling of land is done quickly.”

a3372.speaker: Senior Group Village Head Chimanda
a3372.speech: Commended the government for putting efforts into the development of the scheme, saying it will help end hunger in the area.

a3372.speaker: Tamani Nkhono Mvula, agriculture policy expert
a3372.speech: Said the best time to embark on irrigation farming is now when the rains have just stopped ; called on government to invest more in infrastructure to support irrigation farming, saying most farmers are unable to engage in irrigation farming due to costs involved in setting up irrigation systems: “We need to put the necessary infrastructure in place in order for farmers to be able to embark on irrigation farming. Government should also consider subsidies for irrigation equipment so that farmers are able to afford equipment. Without investing in infrastructure it is very difficult to produce more food through irrigation.”

a3400.speaker: United States of America (official statement for World Malaria Day)
a3400.speech: Stated that over the past decade considerable progress has been made in reducing the burden of malaria mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, and that the U.S. President's Malaria Initiative (PMI) "continues to be a leader in the global fight against malaria" ; said that with host country governments, international donors, U.S. government partners such as the Peace Corps and the Department of Defense, and countless NGOs such as DELIVER and Jhpiego, "we are winning this battle" ; said that PMI has supported Burkina Faso since 2009 and that USAID's support, combined with the efforts of the government and other partners, reduced malaria-related mortality from 9,024 deaths in 2010 to 5,386 in 2014, a 40 percent drop in four years.

a3400.speaker: United States of America (official statement for World Malaria Day)
a3400.speech: "Today, on World Malaria Day, we call on the Government of Burkina Faso and on stakeholders at the local and global levels to accelerate their efforts and investments on behalf of children and women." ; "We must consider collective action to maximize impact, to draw on the skills, interest and resources of the global community to scale up high-impact interventions, and to explore and adapt innovations that can advance health outcomes." ; "With a strong and sustained global commitment from all of us, we can protect communities from malaria and end preventable maternal and child deaths within a generation."

a3400.speaker: World Health Organization
a3400.speech: According to the World Health Organization, the scaling up of malaria control interventions has resulted in an estimated 4.5 million fewer malaria deaths worldwide since 2000.

a3511.speaker: Mesenbet Shenkute, President of the Addis Ababa Chamber of Commerce and Sectoral Association (AACCSA)
a3511.speech: Announced that the inclusive policy recommendation titled ‘Towards the Creation of a Robust Private Sector’ is prepared under the government's strategy which is giving priority for the private sector development ; “The economic policy recommendation was done four months ago and was tabled to the Office of the Prime Minister and other relevant government offices in consideration for the private sector to get better attention under inclusive manner,” adding “we hope all relevant bodies will use it, since it is considering coordinated economic policy” ; said the problems and challenges on the private sector activities have been identified under the document.

a3511.speaker: Getachew Regassa, Secretary of AACCSA
a3511.speech: Said that meanwhile the development of policy will be the accountability of the government, the chamber considered itself responsible to be an instrument to provide support ; “The major reason to develop this policy recommendation is that currently the country is under a transition period that needs support from non-governmental organs. Currently, the government is engaged on massive changes that the chamber needs to put its share in the upcoming strategy for the private sector, and the policy recommendation has also targeted to pressure the government for the benefit of the private sector” ; “Besides focusing on challenges that occur under operation and bureaucracy as we had done in the past, the policy recommendation at the initial stage will have better contribution to address challenges at the grass root level” ; said the policy recommendation has looked at the legal, policy and administration gaps and indicates directions and recommendations ; “Sustainable solution have got priority in our document, meanwhile we have similarities with structural problem that the government frequently stated as a major challenge for the country economic development.”

a3511.speaker: Shibeshi Bettemariam, Deputy Secretary for Advocacy and Innovation at AACCSA
a3511.speech: Adds that the document comprised of 474 pages with two volumes will be an input for the government's development plan ; “Under this plan policy and institutional development recommendations that show the potential of the private sector economic development contribution for the nation are included” ; “The document has 135 policies and institutional development recommendations under key performance indicators with 60 measurements,” “for instance under the pillar of lowering public deficit and debt we raised the formation of legal framework on illicit financing and remittance, indicate recommendations on tax administration, and corporate governance” ; said that some of the points mentioned on the chamber document have similarities with the government's ten year prospective development plan that is currently under discussion and expected to be implemented in the coming decade with two five-year plans.

a3632.speaker: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
a3632.speech: Has reiterated its commitment to tackling the menace of counterfeit and substandard pharmaceutical products in Nigeria.

a3632.speaker: Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC (represented by Bitrus Fraden, Director of Post Marketing Surveillance)
a3632.speech: Said the agency has intensified partnership with countries such as China and India to ensure rigorous testing of products destined for Nigeria; said the strategy includes appointing independent analysts in these countries to verify product safety before shipment; highlighted other proactive measures, including pre-shipment testing, post-marketing surveillance, and consumer engagement. "We are not a dumping ground for substandard products," she said. "Pre-shipment testing ensures that only quality products are sent to Nigeria. This approach reduces waste and prevents counterfeit items from entering our markets."

a3632.speaker: Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC
a3632.speech: Disclosed that 144 batches of substandard pharmaceutical products were recently intercepted and prevented from entering the country, and said these efforts, combined with routine post-marketing inspections and consumer complaints, have helped to reduce the prevalence of harmful products in circulation.

a3632.speaker: Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC
a3632.speech: Stressed the importance of collaboration in achieving NAFDAC's goals, including partnerships with international organisations such as WHO, USAID and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation; said locally NAFDAC is working closely with the Nigeria Customs Service, the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), and the police to enforce regulations and monitor pharmaceutical product distribution. "We need to work as one to protect lives. Unsafe products harm not only consumers but also legitimate businesses. Collaborative efforts are essential to stopping the proliferation of substandard goods," she said.

a3632.speaker: Joseph Kadiri, President of the Association of Nigeria Health Journalists (ANHEJ)
a3632.speech: Said with these ongoing efforts, NAFDAC remains steadfast in its mission to eliminate counterfeit drugs and safeguard public health, and that by leveraging technology, fostering collaboration, and engaging with the public, the agency aims to build a safer and healthier Nigeria.

a3632.speaker: Joseph Kadiri, President of the Association of Nigeria Health Journalists (ANHEJ)
a3632.speech: Said the association holds conferences annually to examine critical health programmes and policies aimed at improving health outcomes for Nigerians; said this year's conference, themed "SWAp Effectiveness in Addressing Poor Health Outcomes: The Role of the Media," is particularly timely given the numerous challenges facing Nigeria's health sector, including inadequate funding, inefficient resource allocation, and poor service delivery, and that the Sector Wide Approach (SWAp) was introduced to address these challenges. "However, the SWAp's effectiveness relies heavily on the active engagement of various stakeholders, including the media. As journalists, we play a vital role in promoting health awareness, education, and advocacy," he said. "Through our reporting, we can hold stakeholders accountable for their actions and policies, provide a platform for marginalised voices to be heard, promote evidence-based health information and best practices, and advocate for policy changes and increased funding for health programmes."

a3742.speaker: Dr Arthur Kobina Kennedy, member of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP)
