a3742.speech: Has criticised President John Dramani Mahama for selectively praising African leaders while ignoring Western contributions to Africa's healthcare sector; noted that President Mahama failed to mention the West spending more than US$157 billion to help Africa and the bilateral assistance from the United States of America and the European Union in the healthcare sector; expressed the concern in a statement issued on September 25, 2025 in response to President Mahama's recent call for Africa to assume leadership in healthcare; added that the summit would have been a good place and time to thank America for the generosity of past governments, starting with Bush and lasting through Biden.

a3742.speaker: Dr Arthur Kobina Kennedy, member of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP)
a3742.speech: On healthcare funding: lamented the lack of commitment from African leaders to healthcare funding, noting that most countries, including Ghana, have not met the Abuja declaration's target of spending 15 per cent of their budgets on health. “A quarter century after the Abuja declaration, most of them, including Ghana, have not even reached eight per cent” ; “Indeed, truth be told, President Mahama's summit was necessitated by what the WHO Director, Tedros Adhanom Gebreyesus, reported as ‘health aid projected to decline by up to 40 per cent this year compared to two years ago’” — a decrease, Dr Kennedy said, due mainly to cuts in global health spending by the Trump administration.

a3742.speaker: Dr Arthur Kobina Kennedy, member of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP)
a3742.speech: On galamsey: urged President Mahama to back his words with action, particularly in addressing the galamsey crisis, which he said posed a significant health risk to Ghanaians. “Show action to back your words by halting galamsey. It is a health emergency and a national crisis.”

a3742.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Gebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a3742.speech: Reported that “health aid [is] projected to decline by up to 40 per cent this year compared to two years ago.”

a3742.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a3742.speech: In his speech at the Africa Health Sovereignty Summit held in Accra on August 5, 2025, praised several African leaders, including President Cyril Ramaphosa of South Africa; former President of Liberia, Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf; President Paul Kagame of Rwanda; former United Nations Secretary General, the late Kofi Annan; former Nigerian leader, Olusegun Obasanjo; and President William Ruto of Kenya, for their leadership in delivery of health services on the continent; called for Africa to assume leadership in healthcare.

a3762.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) (2023 report)
a3762.speech: In its 2023 report, revealed serious dysfunctions in the management of humanitarian aid in the Tindouf camps in Algeria, notably the illegal sale of the UN agency's products on the markets of neighbouring countries.

a3762.speaker: Promotion of Economic and Social Development (PDES), Sahrawi NGO
a3762.speech: On Tuesday in Geneva, alerted the international community to the alarming situation in these camps in south-western Algeria, saying human rights violations there remain a major problem requiring immediate action ; insists on the urgency of taking measures to put an end to these worrying violations, to secure humanitarian corridors, and to offer durable solutions for the inhabitants ; called on the High Commissioner for Human Rights to send a fact-finding mission to closely monitor the situation and provide transparent reports with a view to protecting the rights of the people held there, in accordance with the Geneva Convention relating to Refugees.

a3762.speaker: Fatima Ezzahrae Zouhairi, activist with PDES
a3762.speech: Said, during the 58th session of the Human Rights Council, that thousands of people have been living in these camps in precarious humanitarian conditions for nearly five decades, deprived of their fundamental rights, and that the security situation has also deteriorated recently, with a resurgence of criminal acts and violence, further exacerbating the suffering of the inhabitants ; added that the absence of security and stability, combined with the absence of security and judicial mechanisms on the part of the host country, Algeria, exposes the populations to heightened risks and deprives them of any form of protection or justice ; citing recent reports, stressed that "the geographical isolation of the camps, far from any international monitoring, contributes to the worsening of these violations," and specified that the most vulnerable populations, notably women and children, are particularly exposed to physical and psychological violence as well as to inhumane living conditions.

a3762.speaker: Fatima Ezzahrae Zouhairi, activist with PDES
a3762.speech: "We call on the international community to redouble its efforts to ensure full respect for the human rights of the populations living in the Tindouf camps." She stressed that these efforts must include the provision of unhindered humanitarian aid, guaranteeing freedom of movement for the inhabitants, and putting in place transparent monitoring mechanisms to track these violations and put an end to impunity.

a3809.speaker: Coronel Omar Saranga, Mozambican Defence Ministry spokesman
a3809.speech: confirmed the arrival of South African and Botswana troops, and said these were preparation forces and not the full 3000-soldier SADC contingent. He added that the SADC force commander “is South African and his name is Xolani Mankayi. He is already in Mozambique.”

a3809.speaker: Zimbabwean military sources (anonymous, to NewZimbabwe.com)
a3809.speech: told NewZimbabwe.com (22 July) they received a radio communication advising them that they were now on standby and should await deployment orders.

a3809.speaker: Frederick Shava, Zimbabwean Foreign Minister
a3809.speech: reported to cabinet Tuesday (20 July) that all issues that were holding up their deployment have been ironed out, and a Status of Forces Agreement signed.

a3809.speaker: Carta de Mocambique (report, 21 July)
a3809.speech: reports that Rwandan troops which arrived in Cabo Delgado last week are based at the Total camp on the Afungi peninsula and have started patrols north and south of Palma; also reports (19 July) that the Rwandan commander, Major General Innocent Kabandana, is known for persecuting and murdering opponents of Paul Kagame abroad and claims he was responsible for the elimination of several Rwandan citizens during five years in the USA.

a3809.speaker: Rwandan troops
a3809.speech: claimed to have killed 30 insurgents after encountering a large insurgent group in the forests north of Palma, near the town of Quionga, on Tuesday (20 July).

a3809.speaker: CaboLigado (report, 20 July)
a3809.speech: reports that government troops began informing civilians living in villages on the outskirts of Palma town – Ncumbi, Makongo, Olumbe, and Monjane – that they had until 19 July to relocate to Quitunda, where government forces told civilians they could safely await the results of a planned government/Rwandan offensive in the area, and that they were also barred from traveling by boat.

a3809.speaker: The new district administrator and the local police commissioner of Palma
a3809.speech: told locals at a meeting in Quitunda on 14 July that, while their offices are in Palma town, they will be staying in Quitunda until the planned offensive is over due to security concerns in Palma.

a3809.speaker: Displaced people arriving in Nangade district
a3809.speech: reported that a Mozambican military unit executed 15 suspected insurgents that had been captured attempting to cross the Rovuma River into Tanzania on 13 July.

a3809.speaker: Jambo News (Rwandan newspaper)
a3809.speech: reports that in the 1990s, Kabandana was responsible for the murder of three bishops and nine priests in the DRC and Burundi.

a3809.speaker: Global media investigation consortium and Amnesty International
a3809.speech: revealed this week that Rwanda is one of only two African countries to be using Pegasus spyware from the Israeli NSO group; the consortium and Amnesty gained a list of phone numbers that Pegasus users were targeting, and Rwanda’s targets included President Cyril Ramaphosa.

a3809.speaker: Borges Nhamirre, Institute for Security Studies (19 July report)
a3809.speech: writes that Mozambicans are divided over the Rwandan deployment.

a3809.speaker: Insurgents
a3809.speech: claimed to have killed one soldier and seized three motorcycles in the attack on Namacande, the Muidumbe district capital.

a3809.speaker: Teachers assigned to teach in Macomia district
a3809.speech: are fighting an order to return to work in the district, claiming that it is not yet safe from insurgent attacks, and say they are the only civil servants being ordered back to Macomia, leaving them especially vulnerable.

a3809.speaker: UNHCR
a3809.speech: reports that the price of the Palma-Pemba boat trip has jumped from $25 to $40 per person, and can last 10 days.

a3809.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a3809.speech: announced on 10 June that France is giving up after eight years of unsuccessful attempts to militarily defeat a range of Islamic insurgencies and is withdrawing most of its troops from the Sahel.

a3809.speaker: Prof Jeremy Keenan, Sahel expert (Menas Associates webinar, 21 July)
a3809.speech: explained that France “refused to veer from its insistence on a military counter-insurgency strategy … despite mounting evidence that a military counter-insurgency strategy is not the answer” ; “The solution lies as much with resolving the long term problems – under-development, poverty and poor governance – as it does with military muscle.” ; added that “France’s branding of certain ethic groups as ‘terrorists’ and its subsequent encouragement of their traditional enemies to form auxiliary militias has been a major contributory factor” in escalating conflict and killing.

a3809.speaker: Freedom C. Onuoha, University of Nigeria
a3809.speech: argues that most studies “affirm that the root of maritime insecurity in the Gulf of Guinea stems primarily from bad governance. Despite endowment with vast natural resources, most of the states parade some of the worst indices of human development. These include environmental devastation, high unemployment rates and widespread poverty generated by corruption and bad governance. I also found that unsustainable practices of oil companies have destroyed traditional farming and fishing livelihood systems in coastal communities. This has forced some people to make desperate choices. With declining opportunities for legitimate livelihood amid affluence, some young people in the region take to criminality for survival.”

a3809.speaker: United Nations
a3809.speech: According to the UN there are 740,000 people displaced by the war, more than the population of the war-affected area; the most recent UN access map shows that Bilibiza is only just inside the part of Quissanga district controlled by the insurgents.

a3809.speaker: The Land Report (11 Jan 2021)
a3809.speech: reported that Bill Gates has become the largest private owner of US farmland.

a3809.speaker: Credit Suisse and others
a3809.speech: said to President Armando Guebuza a decade ago that the $2 bn secret debt would guarantee coastal protection as well as huge profits.

a3809.speaker: CIP (Public Integrity Centre) study by Rui Mate, published 20 July
a3809.speech: shows that “a good portion of the concessions” in Cabo Delgado is owned by Mozambique’s political elite – influential people in Frelimo or their families – naming Margarida Talapa (88% of Lurio Ruby Mining), two members of Alberto Chipande’s family, and N’naite Joaquim Chissano; the report is titled “Mining Concession requests increase as armed conflict in Cabo Delgado intensifies: Who are the lords of the mining licenses in Cabo Delgado?”

a3809.speaker: City Press (4 July)
a3809.speech: reported that four spies from South Africa’s State Security Agency (SSA) were caught spying on the Cabo Delgado war and left stranded for nine days in Maputo, with their passports and equipment, including drones, confiscated.

a3809.speaker: News24 (9 July)
a3809.speech: reports that the Mozambican security service SISE shot down one of the South African drones.

a3809.speaker: News24 (17 July 2020), citing insiders
a3809.speech: reported that “insiders said McBride’s key job was to clean up the agency of rogue elements.”

a3809.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a3809.speech: said that the violence in South Africa was pre-planned, which was dismissed by many as claiming conspiracies.

a3809.speaker: Ferial Haffajee, Daily Maverick (14 July)
a3809.speech: investigated in an article “Under investigation: Twelve masterminds planned and executed insurrection on social media, then lost control after looting spree,” work that was enough to convince the BBC (17 July).

a3809.speaker: 2018 Report of the High-Level Review Panel on the SSA
a3809.speech: confirmed that during Jacob Zuma’s years in power, parallel intelligence structures were set up, in effect doing the President’s bidding.

a3809.speaker: Mediafax (21 July)
a3809.speech: reported that in Mozambique the trial of 19 people accused of crimes in relation to the $2 bn secret debt scandal has been set for 23 August.

a3809.speaker: Canal de Mocambique and Carta de Mocambique (21 July)
a3809.speech: reported that the trial will be televised and former President Armando Guebuza will give evidence on 6 October.

a3809.speaker: Mr Justice Robin Knowles, London High Court
a3809.speech: ruled on 21 July that several secret debt cases should be combined into a single hearing next year.

a3809.speaker: US prosecutors investigating the case
a3809.speech: According to US prosecutors, former Finance Minister Manuel Chang received bribes from Privinvest.

a3855.speaker: Diplomatic sources (anonymous)
a3855.speech: have told the Star that Secretary of State Marco Rubio is scheduled to visit Kenya after the initial trip in April was cancelled.

a3855.speaker: Musalia Mudavadi, Prime Cabinet Secretary of Kenya
a3855.speech: said the elevation [of bilateral ties to an “All-Weather Kenya-China Community with a Shared Future for the New Era”] was a landmark development that speaks to the strength, trust and shared vision underpinning the two states' partnership. He added that Kenya had entrenched the One-China policy — the number 1 foreign policy agenda for Beijing — in the revised Kenya Foreign Policy document.

a3855.speaker: Musalia Mudavadi, Prime Cabinet Secretary of Kenya
a3855.speech: said Kenya is well-positioned at the heart of the evolving economic relationship between China and Africa. The ties present a critical chance to recalibrate bilateral trade relations, with an eye on balance, value addition and long-term sustainability, he said ; underscored the importance of concluding discussions on financial cooperation before the end of this month as a critical step forward.

a3855.speaker: Jim Risch, US Senate Foreign Relations Committee chairman
a3855.speech: questioned the close China-Kenya ties, particularly with its US Major Non-NATO Ally designation: “Kenya plays a vital role in regional counterterrorism and stability. But as our newest Major Non-NATO Ally, Kenya's ties with China are troubling.” ; “Widened diplomacy with America's greatest competitor is not an alliance, it's a risk for the US to assess”.

a3855.speaker: General Michael Langley, Commander of the US Africa Command, Marine Corps
a3855.speech: told a media briefing that his second charge from Defence Secretary Hegseth is to confront the military ambitions of the Chinese Communist Party on the Africa continent ; “So while the US works to build transparency and respectful partnerships, China continues to pursue access to Africa's resources, often ignoring long-term sustainability.”

a3855.speaker: Foreign policy analysts
a3855.speech: say Ruto is under pressure to deliver on his campaign promises as domestic pressure mounts on his administration at a time the country is facing cash constraints.

a3855.speaker: Dr Adhere Cavince, China-Africa expert
a3855.speech: says Beijing remains the most promising development partner for Kenya, especially in putting together infrastructure that can reboot economic activities in Kenya ; “China has demonstrated willingness to put capital and technology in partner countries like Kenya.” ; “The rapid infrastructure modernisation under President Uhuru Kenyatta led to Kenya emerging as one of the most successful countries in BRI implementation.” ; “Extension of the SGR and the Mau summit road will dramatically enhance access to western Kenya, foster sustainability of the railway and mobility of people and goods.” ; added that it makes economic sense to work with Chinese partners given their “incredible” edge in both hard and soft infrastructure construction.

a3866.speaker: Government of Zambia
a3866.speech: Government says floods that have hit the country will affect the country’s economic growth.

a3866.speaker: James Mulungushi, Permanent Secretary for Planning and Economic Development, Ministry of Finance and National Planning
a3866.speech: Said the agricultural sector will particularly suffer as a result of floods.

a3866.speaker: James Mulungushi, Permanent Secretary for Planning and Economic Development, Ministry of Finance and National Planning
a3866.speech: He said help from Government to the affected families would continue until they find their own feet ; commended the provincial leadership in Southern Province for acting swiftly to save the affected families ; further cautioned officers involved in the distribution of relief food to the affected families to guard against corruption and ensure that relief food reached the intended families.

a3866.speaker: ZANIS (Zambia News and Information Services)
a3866.speech: ZANIS reports that Dr Mulungushi, who was accompanied by Southern Province Permanent Secretary Darius Hakayobe, was speaking in Kazungula yesterday when he made an on the spot check on the more than 600 displaced Kasaya families.

a3866.speaker: Fred Siansuntwe, Kazungula District Commissioner
a3866.speech: Appealed to Government to supply more relief food to the area.

a3866.speaker: Mungoni Simulilika, Choma District Commissioner
a3866.speech: Said about 700 by 25 kilogramme bags of mealie, food supplements and other relief items will be airlifted from Choma to Namwala and Tezhi Tezhi districts in an exercise that is expected to last about three days ; told ZANIS at the Choma air strip that the humanitarian assistance was testimony of Government’s commitment to alleviating the suffering of flood victims ; said the relief items from the office of the Vice President intended for flood victims in the two districts which have been severely hit by floods are currently stored at the Food Reserve Agency sheds in Choma.

a3930.speaker: “Seville Commitment” (UN outcome document)
a3930.speech: States that the objective now is to “renew the framework of global development financing”, at a moment of “serious geopolitical tensions and conflicts” and when the objectives agreed by the international community in the 2030 Agenda “are seriously behind schedule”; “We are running out of time to achieve our goals and to confront the adverse impacts of climate change. (...) The gap between our sustainable development aspirations and the financing to achieve them has continued to grow, particularly in developing countries, reaching an estimated value of four trillion dollars a year”; the document also emphasises that only the strengthening of multilateralism can respond to the urgent need to eradicate poverty and confront the impacts of climate change, and recognises the sovereign debt of the most vulnerable and developing countries as one of the great obstacles to sustainable development.

a3930.speaker: United Nations (UN figures/accounts)
a3930.speech: According to UN calculations, the current shortfall in development aid is 1.5 billion more than ten years ago, and in 2024 official development assistance fell for the first time in the last six years, with a further 20% fall forecast for 2025.

a3930.speaker: Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs)
a3930.speech: Denounce that the “Seville Commitment” fell short of initial expectations, with many of the demands of developing and most vulnerable countries left out of the final text.

a3930.speaker: The UN and member states
a3930.speech: Consider that it lays the foundations for change and stress that an agreement was reached in a geopolitical context more complicated than ten years ago and marked by tensions in multilateralism.

a3969.speaker: Constitutional Court of South Africa (order published on Tuesday)
a3969.speech: Dismissed Dirco's application for direct access to appeal the order by the Gauteng High Court in Pretoria, which interdicted the government and the African Renaissance and International Cooperation Fund (ARF) from proceeding with humanitarian assistance to Cuba through the fund.

a3969.speaker: Clayson Monyela, Dirco spokesperson (statement)
a3969.speech: Said the decision of the Supreme Court of Appeal petition is still awaited and that the legal proceedings in the review application against the decision to provide humanitarian assistance is continuing in the Gauteng High Court in Pretoria: "In its order, the Constitutional Court did not pronounce itself on the merits of the case, as it was dealing with the application for direct access, which is a procedural matter. The Constitutional Court made it clear in its order that it will not hear the matter at this stage of the process, with the result that the matter should first be ventilated and heard in a different court."

a3969.speaker: Clayson Monyela, Dirco spokesperson
a3969.speech: Said any suggestion that the order given by the Constitutional Court is a "victory" in the case is erroneous: "The substantive matters relating to the review are still to be addressed in the high court process, which is currently ongoing, and all legal routes remain available to the government, including to appeal the matter in the Constitutional Court once the legal proceedings have taken their course."

a3969.speaker: Naledi Pandor, South African Minister of International Relations and Cooperation
a3969.speech: Previously said Cuba faced chronic food, fuel, medicine and electricity shortages.

a3969.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President
a3969.speech: Said health items, and not money, would be donated to Cuba.

a4250.speaker: United States military (announcement)
a4250.speech: On Thursday the North American military announced that it had carried out bombings aimed at destroying the Ras Issa oil port, controlled by the Houthi rebels in Yemen; the US confirms the attack.

a4250.speaker: United States Central Command (statement)
a4250.speech: According to Central Command, the aim of the operation was to destroy the port infrastructure operated by the Houthi militants, which is why the intention was to cut off the fuel supply to the fighters ; “The United States took these measures to eliminate this source of hydrocarbons for the Iran-backed Houthi terrorists and to deprive them of the illegal revenues that have funded their actions to terrorise the whole region for more than a decade,” the command added in a statement.

a4371.speaker: Trump administration (U.S.)
a4371.speech: Has expressed interest in promoting health initiatives focused on economic growth and self-reliance in developing countries; has demonstrated enthusiasm for innovation, particularly in technology; and has favored public-private partnerships.

a4380.speaker: Sarah Kuponiyi, public health development practitioner, social entrepreneur and founder of A Well-Informed Adolescent Initiative (AWIA) and Alora Reusable Pads
a4380.speech: Said that through A Well-Informed Adolescent Initiative (AWIA) and Alora Reusable Pads she has dedicated her career to empowering underserved communities, particularly women and adolescents ; “Since its inception, AWIA has provided comprehensive sexual and reproductive health education to over 15,000 adolescents, addressing issues like teenage pregnancies and unsafe abortions while promoting gender equality.” ; “Over 20,000 reusable pads have been distributed, particularly to marginalised communities, ensuring girls and women no longer miss opportunities due to a lack of sanitary supplies.” ; “My name is Sarah Kuponiyi, but many call me the ‘Pad Queen’ because of my passion for menstrual health equity.” ; “My work is anchored in the belief that empowering young people and women, especially in underserved communities, is critical to creating a more equitable and healthier society.”

a4380.speaker: Sarah Kuponiyi, public health development practitioner, social entrepreneur and founder of A Well-Informed Adolescent Initiative (AWIA) and Alora Reusable Pads
a4380.speech: On her switch from microbiology to public health: “Now, about that career switch – honestly, it wasn’t planned! While studying microbiology at Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), I was trained as a peer health educator and volunteered with a campus-based initiative founded by Professor Segun Fatusi. It was eye-opening.” ; said her NYSC posting to Yala LGA in Cross River State struck her with “the alarming rate of teenage pregnancies, out-of-school adolescents, and teenage mothers unable to return to school” ; “I mobilised adolescents, secured a town hall, and started weekly Friday sessions covering Sexual Reproductive Health education, school reintegration campaigns, and contraceptive awareness. The impact was tangible—more girls returned to school... It was at that moment that I realised public health was my true calling. It was not just a career change; it was a mission.”

a4380.speaker: Sarah Kuponiyi, public health development practitioner, social entrepreneur and founder of A Well-Informed Adolescent Initiative (AWIA) and Alora Reusable Pads
a4380.speech: On her 2024 milestones: “2024 has indeed been phenomenal, and I am incredibly grateful. I feel honoured and humbled by the recognition, but more than anything, they are a call to action. Being recognized means the world sees the impact of my work, and it fuels my drive to do even more. It is a reminder that there is so much left to achieve for gender equality, menstrual and reproductive health.”

a4380.speaker: Sarah Kuponiyi, public health development practitioner, social entrepreneur and founder of A Well-Informed Adolescent Initiative (AWIA) and Alora Reusable Pads
a4380.speech: On the African Union Beijing +30 Africa CSO Review and the Mandela Washington Fellowship: “Being part of the African Union Beijing +30 Africa CSO Review was powerful. As a National Gender Youth Activist for UN Women since 2020, I have contributed to gender equality through regional discussions, policy blueprints, and feminist manifestos.” ; “For the Mandela Washington Fellowship, I was selected for the Business Leadership track at Jackson State University. This program was transformative, blending leadership training with practical skills for scaling my business.” ; “These experiences highlight the importance of amplifying local solutions on global platforms, especially for marginalised groups.”

a4380.speaker: Sarah Kuponiyi, public health development practitioner, social entrepreneur and founder of A Well-Informed Adolescent Initiative (AWIA) and Alora Reusable Pads
a4380.speech: On Ambassador Linda Thomas-Greenfield’s shout-out: “Oh, it was surreal! Imagine being in a room with 700 outstanding African leaders and suddenly getting spotlighted by Ambassador Linda Greenfield Thomas. I did not see it coming. It was a moment of pride, not just for me but for the work I do in Nigeria – advancing menstrual health and empowering youth. I am deeply grateful for her recognition; it reminds me to keep going, even when the work gets tough.”

a4380.speaker: Sarah Kuponiyi, public health development practitioner, social entrepreneur and founder of A Well-Informed Adolescent Initiative (AWIA) and Alora Reusable Pads
a4380.speech: On her books Teens Blueprint and My Period: “These books are more than just educational materials— they are interactive tools that make learning fun and relatable. With engaging stories, activities, and reflection prompts, they provide comprehensive sex education in a way that resonates with adolescents. Thanks to the USAID ICHSSA Project in Nigeria, these books have reached over 20,000 young people, equipping them with knowledge and breaking barriers to sexual health education.”

a4380.speaker: Sarah Kuponiyi, public health development practitioner, social entrepreneur and founder of A Well-Informed Adolescent Initiative (AWIA) and Alora Reusable Pads
a4380.speech: On her Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene early career research grant: “Winning the Early Career Research Grant was a milestone for me as a menstrual health advocate. It allowed me to research Assessing and Enhancing Menstrual Health and Hygiene Policies: A Comparative Analysis in English-Speaking West African Countries. This project focused on addressing policy gaps to improve menstrual health access and outcomes. The grant reinforced my passion for evidence-based advocacy and how research can drive policy change, especially for marginalised groups.”

a4380.speaker: Sarah Kuponiyi, public health development practitioner, social entrepreneur and founder of A Well-Informed Adolescent Initiative (AWIA) and Alora Reusable Pads
a4380.speech: On the Chevening Scholarship: “The Chevening Scholarship was a pivotal moment in my career. It enabled me to pursue a Master’s in Public Health at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, where I deepened my expertise in Sexual Reproductive Health. The program broadened my understanding of global health systems and equipped me with the tools to design innovative solutions for low-resource settings. I’m immensely grateful to the FCDO and the UK government for this life-changing opportunity.”

a4380.speaker: Sarah Kuponiyi, public health development practitioner, social entrepreneur and founder of A Well-Informed Adolescent Initiative (AWIA) and Alora Reusable Pads
a4380.speech: Advice to young leaders in Nigeria: “start where you are, use what you have, and keep going. Making an impact does not always require grand resources or titles – it starts with recognizing the challenges around you and taking small, consistent steps to address them.” ; “Surround yourself with people who inspire and challenge you, seek mentors, and never stop learning... Above all, take care of yourself. Burnout is real... Lastly, do not let fear of failure stop you. Every setback is a lesson, and every lesson is a step closer to success. Together, we are shaping a better Nigeria – one bold step at a time.”

a4520.speaker: Wilhelmina Diop, Group CEO of HelloSolar
a4520.speech: Confirmed that HelloSolar is currently running a pilot project, in partnership with BelCash, Shell Foundation, DFID, USAID and Power Africa, to test its PAYGO model with end-to-end distribution, installation and after sales services.

a4520.speaker: Mountaga Vince Diop, founder and CEO of BelCash
a4520.speech: "We're very happy to participate in enabling the first PAYGO and international remittance payment" with HelloSolar in Ethiopia and contribute to giving access to affordable energy solutions to the Ethiopian off-grid population."

a4520.speaker: Osman Ibrahim, Country Director of HelloSolar Ethiopia
a4520.speech: "In addition to making our solar home systems affordable through PAYGO, we also make sure to provide best-in-class services with our end-to-end distribution, installation and after sales services."

a4520.speaker: Bart Minsaer, General Manager, HelloSolar
a4520.speech: "After the pilot project, HelloSolar will adapt and roll out its model nationwide and be at the prime position to achieve the Ethiopian government's target of providing 3.5 million solar home systems by 2025."

a4520.speaker: Michael Tesfaye Hiruy, HelloSolar Chief Strategy Officer
a4520.speech: "Our mission goes beyond providing affordable access to energy" ... "moving forward, we will forge the necessary partnerships to provide access to connectivity through affordable smartphones and digital services such as healthcare, education, market access and employment".

a4521.speaker: Congolese presidency
a4521.speech: Reported that President Félix Tshisekedi is expected to present the DRC's position and express his government's expectations, and that his intervention, expected to come last, will deal with the urgent measures needed to restore peace, notably an immediate ceasefire, condemnation of foreign interventions, the withdrawal of non-governmental forces from Congolese territory and the reopening of Goma airport in order to deliver humanitarian aid.

a4521.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, Tanzanian President and host of the meeting
a4521.speech: Opened the summit by calling for collective action to respond to the security challenges in the DRC; stressed the importance of a coordinated and inclusive approach, guaranteeing the country's sovereignty and a durable return to peace.

a4521.speaker: William Ruto, Kenyan President and current chair of the EAC
a4521.speech: Warned against the worsening of the humanitarian situation because of the persistent violence; pleaded for an immediate ceasefire, judging that a halt to hostilities was necessary to open the way to political dialogue and lasting stabilisation.

a4521.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, Zimbabwean President and current chair of SADC
a4521.speech: Insisted on the importance of a diplomatic approach and warned against an exclusively military solution; denounced outside influences that complicate the resolution of the conflict and called for a collective commitment by African states to guarantee the region's stability.

a4533.speaker: Government Annual Economic Report (Malawi, official records)
a4533.speech: Shows that tobacco raked in about $545 million in 2024, up from $389.3 million in 2023; that pulses exports improved to $81 million from $62.8 million and tea rose from $62.6 million to $68.7 million; and that the goods balance deteriorated by 4.9 percent, with the deficit widening from close to $2.2 billion in 2023 to near $2.3 billion in 2024: “This was primarily driven by a 2.8 percent increase in goods imports, which rose from 3.145 billion in 2023 to $3.234 billion in 2024, coupled with a 1.9 percent decline in goods exports, from $965 million to $946 million” ; further explains that the increase in imports was fueled by high demand for vehicles, petroleum oil, pharmaceuticals, and farm inputs, while the decline in exports was mainly attributed to a decline in sugar production.

a4533.speaker: Tobacco Commission (TC)
a4533.speech: Acknowledged good market trends in recent years as global demand continues to improve owing to production slumps in some countries.

a4533.speaker: Telephorus Chigwenembe, Tobacco Commission spokesperson
a4533.speech: Said the outlook is promising: “We are happy that the crop we regulate is doing well considering the improving exports as the figures show. We hope this trend continues to ensure farmers have a stable market.”

a4533.speaker: Government of Malawi (projections)
a4533.speech: Projects the goods account deficit to widen further in 2025, increasing by 3.84 percent, from $1.85 billion to $1.9 billion, with both exports and imports of goods expected to grow, by 15 percent and 8 percent, respectively.

a4533.speaker: Minister of Agriculture of Malawi
a4533.speech: Has indicated increased efforts to boost the country’s exports through the use of the mega farms initiative, targeting China for soya, India for pigeon peas and central Africa for pulses.

a4542.speaker: Prof. Dr. Layli Maparyan, President of the University of Liberia
a4542.speech: Confirmed to the Liberian Senate Committee on Education the retirement plans for lecturers and professors, saying the move is intended to reduce financial cost and save resources, and that the initiative aims to align with Liberian law, which mandates retirement at age 60, though she noted academia often allows experienced individuals to continue teaching beyond this statutory age. “We will implement reductions by retiring those who have reached the age limit, as the retirement age in Liberia is 60. However, in academia, individuals can continue to teach beyond this age. We will also remove ghost names.”

a4542.speaker: Prof. Dr. Layli Maparyan, President of the University of Liberia
a4542.speech: Disclosed that the University will need approximately US$3.9 million for total renovation, included in the US$41 million budget presented to the Legislature, of which only US$33 million was received, 90 percent of it for salaries. “It will cost $3.9 million to renovate the University of Liberia, and an additional $300,000 is needed for bathroom renovations. We requested a budget of $41 million, but we only received $33 million. However, 90% of the $33 million has been allocated for salaries.”

a4542.speaker: Senator Nathaniel McGill, Margibi County Senator, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Education
a4542.speech: Requested comprehensive administrative and academic plans from each official for the current budget year.

a4542.speaker: Purported University of Liberia Faculty and Staff listing as of June 2025 (list obtained by The New Dawn)
a4542.speech: Indicates that the cost-saving measure is allegedly being proposed by the Interim Vice President for Finance and Fiscal Affairs, Dr. Lester Tenny, pending approval of UL President Dr. Ophelia Maparyan; the list contains names of lecturers and professors, their dates of employment, dates of birth, gender, and current ages.

a4542.speaker: Critics (unnamed)
a4542.speech: Accused Dr. Maparyan of ulterior motives, alleging that nearly 50 individuals previously made redundant by USAID have been “imported” into the University of Liberia's faculty with ranks from Assistant to Associate Professor, and that experienced faculty are being prematurely retired to accommodate them; argued the affected individuals represent decades of institutional knowledge and that their forced retirement would be a direct blow to academic freedom, institutional memory, and the quality of education at UL. “The intent behind this scheme is to weaken independent voices within the faculty ranks, accommodate loyalists who owe their positions to Dr. Maparyan's patronage. Also, this is intended to erode the integrity and autonomy of the University of Liberia as a public academic institution. Lastly, if this agenda succeeds, the University risks becoming an institution run by favoritism rather than merit, undermining its credibility nationally and internationally.”

a4542.speaker: One of the potential victims of the pending retirement exercise (anonymous UL faculty member)
a4542.speech: Said the recent developments at the University of Liberia reveal a troubling scheme by the current administration under Dr. Ophelia Maparyan; according to him, a list of active, qualified and experienced faculty members is being quietly prepared for premature retirement, a move that appears less about academic reform and more about creating space for new appointees whose loyalty will be directed to Dr. Maparyan personally rather than to the University, setting a dangerous precedent for political patronage and the personal consolidation of power within an academic environment.

a4542.speaker: Cllr. Noris Tweah, Vice President for University Relations, University of Liberia
a4542.speech: Said he could not speak to the matter: “Lincoln, it's after working hours, and I am on the tennis court right now. I am telling you that I am on the tennis court right now, and it's after working hours. The University is only paying me for the hours I work. I had a long day today. I am on the tennis court playing game, so I can't talk now”; contacted again on Tuesday, September 2, 2025 via direct calls and text messages, he declined to comment.

a4838.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a4838.speech: reaffirmed Mozambique's commitment to consolidating relations with the United States of America, during the audience granted to Ambassador Peter Hendrick Vrooman.

a4838.speaker: Peter Hendrick Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a4838.speech: in statements to the press, highlighted the solidity of the partnership between the two countries, the new opportunities in the private sector and North American investments in strategic areas such as gas, health and infrastructure; said the audience with the Head of State was an opportunity not only to revisit the past of the bilateral relationship, but also to look to the future with enthusiasm; highlighted "the importance of the investment of almost five billion US dollars in the gas area"; underlined the importance of investments in infrastructure as a basis for sustainable economic growth.

a4838.speaker: Peter Hendrick Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a4838.speech: said cooperation between the two countries goes beyond the energy sector, equally covering social and humanitarian areas, and gave special emphasis to the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), describing it as "a programme that saves the lives of many people in the country."

a4838.speaker: Peter Hendrick Vrooman, US Ambassador to Mozambique
a4838.speech: expressed appreciation for the spirit of resilience and hope he found in Mozambique, praising President Chapo's optimistic vision: "I think that his optimism is very important. As the National Anthem says, 'stone by stone building the new day'. And this idea, I think we will work in that direction, and we are together" ; asked about the future of bilateral relations: "I think so. And even when I finish my mission, we will continue."

a4917.speaker: Christian Tetteh Yohuno, COP, Inspector General of Police of Ghana
a4917.speech: Declared an all-out war on illegal mining, also known as ‘galamsey’, because it poses a serious threat to national security and the environment ; revealed that armed criminals linked to illegal mining operations have carried out brutal attacks on innocent civilians, including forest guards, without justification: “This lawlessness must not be allowed to continue” ; stressed that urgent action was needed to combat the problem: “We are declaring war on illegal mining, and I expect every regional commander to take decisive action, to bring perpetrators to justice.”

a4917.speaker: myjoyonline.com (report)
a4917.speech: Reported that the Inspector General of Police has declared an all-out war on illegal mining because it poses a serious threat to national security and the environment.

a4917.speaker: Emmanuel Armah Kofi Buah, Minister for Lands and Natural Resources of Ghana
a4917.speech: Said that last year alone, excavators worth GHS6.2billion were imported into the country, making it the third largest import into the country within the period being referenced.

a4976.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS)
a4976.speech: is relieved to learn of the release on bail of Goobjoog Media Group deputy director, Abdiaziz Ahmed Gurbiye, on Saturday 18 April 2020 and calls for the Somali government to free Radio Hiigsi editor, Mohamed Abduwahaab Nuur (also known as Abuuja).

a4976.speaker: Federal Government of Somalia
a4976.speech: has noted with serious concern the spreading of false and misleading information regarding Somalia's National Intelligence and Security Agency (NISA) published by The Star (Kenya) and Standard media (Kenya).

a4976.speaker: Amnesty International
a4976.speech: is calling on the Somaliland authorities to immediately and unconditionally release detained journalist Abdimalik Muse Oldon, who was arrested and arbitrarily detained a year ago for exercising his right to freedom of expression; Amnesty International is concerned.

a4976.speaker: Al-Shabaab's propaganda media and security observers
a4976.speech: confirmed that the Al-Shabaab militant group on Wednesday executed six young men over allegations of espionage in Jamame town in the southern Somalia region of Lower Jubba.

a4976.speaker: National Union of Somali Journalists (NUSOJ)
a4976.speech: has published new guidance (advices) setting out how journalists and media houses in Somalia can meet their media duties as they navigate the effects of the coronavirus pandemic.

a5301.speaker: Molise Ramaili, LNDC Interim CEO
a5301.speech: highlighted that sometime last year Ace Apparel faced a closure bringing a challenge of unemployment to so many Basotho; the worst-case scenario was its closure during the Christmas holidays where employees would have been left without their salaries. Ramaili mentioned that they sat down and figured a way out. He said they approached Joans Enterprise bringing along investors from South Africa noting to them that Basotho are experts in sewing and are always ready to do a great job. He said if it were not for Basotho's hard work, investors would not stay and would have searched for market elsewhere. "We promised investors to give them a firm that will do a great job and in return we pleaded with them to give the same firm work so as to grow. This is a huge change in terms of opening factories to see to it that Basotho are employed through this campaign," he said ; highlighted that their journey with the investors and Joans was a success as the factory grew from 180 employees to 350 and now it has employed 700 Basotho.

a5301.speaker: Molise Ramaili, LNDC Interim CEO
a5301.speech: noted that the management has informed that they have not stopped employing and it is their wish to expand once again and employ more Basotho; the issue of expansion is important especially in factories, adding they attract investors. "We are already selecting another factory that was called CMT where Joans Enterprise will expand and be able to employ 700 more Basotho. The issue of opening factories has been taken into serious consideration and this will go a long way so that Basotho are employed. I urge workers and management to continue working hard, as the LNDC we will continue supporting them and where they have challenges we are ready to solve them together so that the factory stays sustainable," he said.

a5301.speaker: Mokhethi Shelile, Trade Minister
a5301.speech: noted that there are challenges such as unemployment which lead to Basotho leaving the country and seeking work elsewhere. He said one example was the sudden closure of the Ace Apparel which left many factory workers stranded without work. The minister was appreciative Joans came along and assisted ; he urged workers to work hard all the time and to be a part of unions because the ministry of trade and the ministry of labour usually work together with unions ; exchanged a vote of thanks to Joans Management for their efforts to continue employing Basotho and alleviating the high unemployment rate.

a5301.speaker: Mokhethi Shelile, Trade Minister
a5301.speech: said the government is waiting for tariffs announcement at least until September after doing all the necessary requirements to be a part of the Southern African countries that can work with the United States in terms of market. He also spoke about the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) which he cautioned will be ending, adding that government is working towards finding tariffs agreement that does not exceed 10 percent to enable market access in USA. Shelile also noted that the government is in search of alternative market access in other countries.

a5301.speaker: Manoj Rooplall, Joans Enterprise Cutting Room Manager
a5301.speech: exchanged a vote of thanks to the ministry for assisting with the building so that the company could grow and increase employment. He said they look forward to the future growth with the support of the Lesotho government in the textile industry. He likewise thanked customers, and stakeholders.

a5301.speaker: Selinah Mpakathe, Joans Enterprise Floor Manager
a5301.speech: added that for a firm which commenced as an SME with only 180 employees, moving to 700 by March this year is a huge step and it is promising for many other Basotho in terms of employment opportunities. She noted with appreciation the Management for continuing to search for investors to create jobs in Lesotho.

a5301.speaker: 'Makatleho Mothae, an employee
a5301.speech: highlighted that she was an employee at Ace Apparel and was part of those who were retrenched. She noted that through Joans Enterprise she is now back to work. She hoped more factories will be opened so that those on queues outside also receive the opportunity to be able to feed their families as employees.

a5332.speaker: George Weah, former President of Liberia and Congress for Democratic Change (CDC) leader
a5332.speech: Extended peace and said there is no reason to justify his relationship with the late former Liberian First Lady ; “Do not let People divide us, we are one family, and every Liberian is my family. So, do not let people deceive you to cause confusion among us. We are all one family. And there is no need to justify how I treated our mother, but I know I treated her with respect and honor.”

a5332.speaker: Veronica Mamie Doe, elder daughter of the late President Samuel Doe
a5332.speech: Smashed Mr. Weah for what she describes as hypocrisy and the neglect of her mother when she needed him most; vowed that the former President should come nowhere near her mother’s funeral activities; reiterated that the family does not need the gift from the former President ; “Don’t pretend to care about her in death when you didn’t listen to her in life” ; “I’m the elder daughter of this family, and in consultation with my siblings, we have agreed that the gift be returned to Mr. Weah. During his presentation, there were choice of words he made that didn’t go down well with us, plus all that he has done to our mother. I personally returned the gift, and I’m not aware that these items have been brought back.” ; “And right now, as I Speak, it will be taken away. It doesn’t belong here.” ; “Mr. Weah never showed concern for our mother when she was alive. Now that she’s gone, he wants to make a gesture. We see that as dishonest and ungrateful.”

a5332.speaker: Dr. Isaac Nyenebo, liaison between Doe’s family and visiting sympathizers
a5332.speech: Expressed regret and formally accepted the gift on behalf of the family ; “In every given situation, there is misunderstanding, but this under resolution already, you know, when a leader dies, there’s this form of misunderstanding. But at the end of the day, we all come together to have a befitting burial of our mother.” ; gave assurance that despite the pulling and hauling between rejection and acceptance of the condolence package, the Doe’s family had resolved to accept the gift ; “You know all of us are disturbed by the departure of our mother. But in every family, you have elders, and people listen to their elders. We are resolved to give our mother a befitting burial.”

a5332.speaker: The Doe family
a5332.speech: Has long maintained that the late Nancy B. Doe, widow of former President Samuel K. Doe, was denied her rightful benefits as a former First Lady during Mr. Weah’s administration, a matter they say remains unresolved.

a5403.speaker: Somaliland (breakaway region of Somalia)
a5403.speech: Has rejected an attempt by the central government to give the US exclusive control of a port and airbase in Berbera, saying the facilities are not Mogadishu's to give away.

a5403.speaker: Abdirahman Dahir Aden, Somaliland's Foreign Affairs Minister
a5403.speech: Dismissed the move as "desperate" ; "There is nothing they can do to stop the upcoming recognition of Somaliland," he posted on X in response to the letter ; "The USA is not stupid. They know who they need to deal with when it comes to Berbera port," the minister told Reuters.

a5403.speaker: Letter from the Somali government to President Trump (dated 16 March)
a5403.speech: Explains how exclusive control of the offered airbases and ports could help the US counter the influence of other international players in the Horn of Africa: "These strategically positioned assets provide an opportunity to bolster American engagement in the region... while preventing external competitors from establishing a presence in this critical corridor."

a5403.speaker: Reuters
a5403.speech: Says the letter to Trump is dated 16 March.

a5403.speaker: Officials in Puntland
a5403.speech: Have yet to comment on the letter.

a5403.speaker: Garowe Online (Somali publication)
a5403.speech: Says that if the offer [of the port of Bosaso] was made without consulting Puntland officials, relations between Puntland and Mogadishu may be further strained.

a5403.speaker: Somalia (federal government)
a5403.speech: Responded to Ethiopia's maritime deal with Somaliland by calling the move an "act of aggression", as it regards Somaliland as part of its territory.

a5525.speaker: Mulenga Musepa, Statistician General, Zambia Statistics Agency (ZamStats)
a5525.speech: “Annual inflation for January 2024 increased to 13.2 percent from 13.1 percent recorded in December, 2023. The price of a 25kg bag of roller mealie meal increased by 2.05 percent from K239.53 to K244.44.” ; “The monthly national average price of a 20-litre tin of maize grain increased by 9.49 percent from K145.99 to K159.84.”

a5525.speaker: Mulenga Musepa, Statistician General, ZamStats
a5525.speech: Said the country in 2023 recorded a trade surplus of K6.2 billion, compared to K44.5 billion recorded in 2022; also stated that Zambia recorded a trade surplus of K0.7 billion in December 2023 compared to a deficit of K0.6 billion in November 2023 ; “Exports mainly comprising domestically produced goods, increased by 14.6 percent to K21.1 billion in December 2023 from K18.4 billion in November 2023. This was mainly on account of 21.4 percent increase in export earnings from Intermediate goods, respectively.” ; “Imports increased by 7.4 percent to K20.4 billion in December 2023 from K19.0 billion in November 2023. This was mainly as a result of 16.8 and 9.6 percent increases in import bills of consumer goods and Intermediate goods, respectively.”

a5626.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (internal memo to staff)
a5626.speech: "No new funds shall be obligated for new awards or extensions of existing awards until each proposed new award or extension has been reviewed and approved."

a5626.speaker: US State Department memo
a5626.speech: Said waivers have so far been approved by Rubio for "foreign military financing for Israel and Egypt and administrative expenses, including salaries, necessary to administer foreign military financing" ; allowed the State Department to make other case-by-case exceptions and temporarily to fund salaries to staff and other administrative expenses, and called for an internal review of all foreign assistance within 85 days.

a5626.speaker: USAID official (anonymous)
a5626.speech: Said officers responsible for projects in Ukraine have been told to stop all work, and that among the frozen projects are support to schools and health assistance like emergency maternal care and childhood vaccinations ; "Organisations will have to stop all activities, so all lifesaving health services, HIV/AIDS, nutrition, maternal and child health, all agriculture work, all support of civil society organisations, education."

a5626.speaker: Lawmakers from the Democratic Party
a5626.speech: Said that more than 20 million people relied on medication through PEPFAR and 63 million people on US-funded anti-malaria efforts including nets.

a5626.speaker: Representative Gregory Meeks, top Democrat on the House Foreign Relations Committee, and Representative Lois Frankel (letter)
a5626.speech: "For years, Republicans in Congress have decried what they see as a lack of US credibility vis-a-vis countries like China, Russia, and Iran" ; "Now our credibility is on the line, and it appears we will cut and run from American commitments to our partners around the world." They also noted that foreign assistance is appropriated by Congress and said they would seek its implementation.

a5626.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a5626.speech: Wrote, in justifying the freeze, that it was impossible for the new administration to assess whether existing foreign aid commitments "are not duplicated, are effective and are consistent with President Trump's foreign policy."

a5626.speaker: Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (data)
a5626.speech: According to the OECD, the United States gave more than $64 billion in overseas development assistance in 2023, the last year for which records were available.

a5626.speaker: Oxfam
a5626.speech: Said that Trump was abandoning a longstanding consensus in the United States for foreign assistance.

a5626.speaker: Abby Maxman, Oxfam America president (statement)
a5626.speech: "Humanitarian and development assistance accounts for only around one percent of the federal budget; it saves lives, fights diseases, educates millions of children and reduces poverty." ; "Suspending and ultimately cutting many of these programs could have life or death consequences for countless children and families who are living through crisis."

a5738.speaker: Governments and international non-governmental organisations
a5738.speech: Warned that the Palestinians no longer have anywhere to go.

a5738.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a5738.speech: Insists on the idea of an operation in Rafah, alleging the need to eradicate Hamas, and without giving details about the fate of the population; on Sunday he confirmed the imminent entry of military forces into the city of Rafah to finish off “the battalions that remain of Hamas”, and insisted that the civilian population of that city must “abandon” the area, with or without the help of international humanitarian organisations.

a5738.speaker: Israel Defence Forces (IDF)
a5738.speech: Said they had carried out “a series of attacks against terrorist targets in the Shabura area.”

a5738.speaker: Government of Israel
a5738.speech: Asked the UN to “cooperate” in the “withdrawal” of civilians in the combat zones in the Gaza Strip, including the city of Rafah; also pointed to “a cover-up of Hamas's militarisation of hospitals and military assets inside United Nations facilities”, referring to the discovery of a tunnel beneath UNRWA's main headquarters in Gaza.

a5738.speaker: Eylon Levy, spokesman for the Israeli government
a5738.speech: Criticised the UN agencies for “having been transferring civilians to Hamas strongholds and validating Hamas's 'human shields' strategy”, and argued: “The war can end quickly, without further suffering, if Hamas surrenders immediately, lays down its weapons, releases the hostages and brings its war criminals to justice. All actors dedicated to protecting civilians and improving humanitarian conditions in Gaza should call on Hamas to surrender now, instead of pressing Hamas to keep its four battalions standing in the face of an imminent Israeli victory.”

a5738.speaker: Philippe Lazzarini, Commissioner-General of UNRWA
a5738.speech: Stressed that the agency's staff “left the headquarters in Gaza City on 12 October, following evacuation orders issued by Israel and in the face of intensifying bombardment in the area”, and called for an “independent” investigation.

a5738.speaker: Israel Katz, Israeli Foreign Minister
a5738.speech: Called for Lazzarini's resignation.

a5738.speaker: Hamas
a5738.speech: Warned that any operation by Israeli forces in Rafah would threaten the negotiations for the release of hostages in exchange for Palestinian prisoners and would constitute a “catastrophe and a global massacre.”

a5738.speaker: Government of Gaza
a5738.speech: Recalled that 1.5 million Palestinians currently live in the province of Rafah, of whom 1.3 million were displaced by violence in other parts of the enclave, which “foreshadows a great catastrophe”, and accused Israel of having already carried out “thousands of massacres in the rest of the provinces of the Gaza Strip during the current war of genocide.”

a5738.speaker: Mahmoud Abbas, President of the Palestinian Authority
a5738.speech: Said on Friday that the Israeli plan to expand the offensive on Rafah is part of the strategy to “displace the Palestinian people from their lands” and appealed for the international community to act to prevent it.

a5738.speaker: United Nations, led by Antonio Guterres
a5738.speech: Has appealed several times for an end to the conflict and warned that an Israeli military operation in Rafah would aggravate the “humanitarian nightmare” of the local population, with “incalculable regional consequences.”

a5738.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a5738.speech: Asked Netanyahu on Monday to guarantee the safety of the 1.5 million Palestinians concentrated in Rafah, reaffirming the view that a military operation should not proceed without a credible and feasible plan to ensure the safety and support of the more than one million people sheltering there; indicated that Washington will not support an operation on such a large scale, reaffirmed the “common objective” of seeing Hamas defeated, and called for “urgent and specific measures to increase the volume and consistency of humanitarian assistance to innocent Palestinian civilians.”

a5738.speaker: Josep Borrell, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs
a5738.speech: Referred to the announced Rafah action as “an indescribable humanitarian catastrophe.”

a5738.speaker: Recep Tayyip Erdogan, President of Turkey
a5738.speech: Asked the UN Security Council on Monday to “control Israel” after the recent attacks on the city of Rafah.

a5738.speaker: Netherlands (government)
a5738.speech: Announced the suspension of the export of warplane parts to Israel.

a5738.speaker: Egypt (government)
a5738.speech: Threatened to break the peace treaty with Israel if Israeli troops are sent to Rafah, stating that it would sanction the suspension of the peace treaty if Israeli troops attack the densely populated border city, and warning that the fighting could force the closure of the main route for supplying humanitarian aid to the besieged territory.

a5738.speaker: Saudi Arabia
a5738.speech: Condemned Netanyahu's plans and called for an urgent meeting of the Security Council to avert an “imminent humanitarian catastrophe.”

a5738.speaker: China and Russia
a5738.speech: Have limited themselves to repeating the idea of a ceasefire between the parties.

a5738.speaker: Iran
a5738.speech: Called for Israel's exclusion from the UN, again expressing support for the Palestinian cause, victim of “crimes against humanity.”

a5738.speaker: Amnesty International
a5738.speech: Said it has “new evidence” that Israel's “unlawful attacks” in the Gaza Strip have caused “an enormous number of civilian casualties” and that there is “a real risk of genocide”, in which Israeli troops “continue to disregard international humanitarian law, destroying entire families with total impunity.”

a5827.speaker: Fuad Ahmed Nuh, Somaliland’s Minister of Civil Aviation and Airports Development
a5827.speech: "This investment goes beyond infrastructure; it represents a commitment to enhanced connectivity, economic development and the long-term prosperity of our nation," Nuh wrote on X ; Nuh added that the project carries the promise of turning Somaliland’s primary hub into a more reliable and competitive gateway.

a5827.speaker: Somaliland Ministry of Civil Aviation and Airports Development (statement)
a5827.speech: The ministry said construction would begin within six months in phases to avoid major disruption, positioning the project as the most significant investment in Somaliland’s aviation infrastructure to date ; in a statement, the ministry said the project is "the largest investment ever made in Somaliland’s aviation infrastructure, and the second-largest foreign investment after DP World."

a5827.speaker: Some Somaliland commentators and social media users
a5827.speech: Have raised doubts about the firm’s very existence.

a5827.speaker: Somaliland officials (non-response)
a5827.speech: Somaliland officials have not yet responded to requests for documentation confirming the company’s legal status, ownership, or track record.

a5988.speaker: Bill Gates, Microsoft founder
a5988.speech: Said he intends to give away 99 per cent of his vast fortune over the next 20 years and would accelerate his giving via his foundation, with plans to end its operations in 2045; said his foundation has already given $100bn (£75bn) towards health and development projects and that he expects it will spend another $200bn, depending on markets and inflation, over the next two decades, drawing from its endowment ; “People will say a lot of things about me when I die, but I am determined that ‘he died rich’ will not be one of them,” he wrote in a blog post Thursday ; In the post he outlined three main goals for his foundation: eliminating preventable diseases which kill mothers and children; eliminating infectious diseases including malaria and measles; and eliminating poverty for hundreds of millions of people; he also said he has been inspired to give away money by investor Warren Buffett and other philanthropists.

a5988.speaker: Andrew Carnegie, tycoon (1889 essay ‘The Gospel of Wealth’, quoted by Gates)
a5988.speech: “the man who dies thus rich dies disgraced.”

a5988.speaker: Bloomberg
a5988.speech: According to Bloomberg, the Microsoft founder is the fifth-richest person in the world.

a5988.speaker: Bill Gates, Microsoft founder (on foreign aid cuts and Elon Musk)
a5988.speech: Criticised the US, UK and France for cutting their foreign aid budgets ; “It’s unclear whether the world’s richest countries will continue to stand up for its poorest people. But the one thing we can guarantee is that, in all of our work, the Gates Foundation will support efforts to help people and countries pull themselves out of poverty” ; In an interview with the Financial Times he accused Tesla CEO and Department of Government Efficiency boss Elon Musk of being personally responsible for the deaths of children through his cuts to the US aid budget, including the dismantling of the US Agency for International Development ; “The picture of the world’s richest man killing the world’s poorest children is not a pretty one” ; “I’d love for [Musk] to go in and meet the children that have now been infected with HIV because he cut that money.”

a5988.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5988.speech: Erroneously claimed that cancelled grants to a hospital in Gaza Province, Mozambique, were funding condoms “for Hamas” in the Gaza Strip.

a5988.speaker: Elon Musk, Tesla CEO and Department of Government Efficiency boss
a5988.speech: Later acknowledged the claim was wrong and said “we will make mistakes”, however the cost-cutting continued.

a6031.speaker: Axel Cramer, president of the Namibia Professional Hunting Association (Napha)
a6031.speech: According to Napha president Axel Cramer, both hunting expos were a tremendous success, with Namibia's flag flying high in the US. "About 30 Namibian exhibitors participated in Nashville from Wednesday to Saturday. Some of our Napha members confirmed there was significant interest, particularly in big-game hunting trips for elephants, crocodiles and buffaloes, but not as much for plains game," Cramer told Network Media Hub (NMH) from Nashville ; added that there was strong competition from Africa at the expos, particularly from South Africa, Tanzania and Zambia.

a6115.speaker: Dr Stanford Ndibalema, Assistant Director of Veterinary Services at the Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries (Tanzania)
a6115.speech: Emphasized the importance of collaboration in combating rabies: “The partnership between USAID and the Tanzanian government is crucial in our fight against rabies. By working together, we can ensure that communities are not only educated about the risks but also empowered to take proactive steps in protecting themselves and their pets.” ; Underscored the critical need for vaccination and community awareness campaigns, highlighting that “every vaccinated dog is a step toward a rabies-free community.”

a6115.speaker: Revina, a mother of three from Mwanza
a6115.speech: Recounted her experience: “Before the campaign, I had no idea how dangerous rabies could be. Once we learned about the importance of vaccinating our dogs, we took immediate action. Now, I feel much safer allowing my children to play outside.”

a6166.speaker: NGO Regulatory Authority (NGORA)
a6166.speech: Has exposed the alarming truth behind the operations of many Non-Governmental Organizations in Malawi — funds meant for community development are being siphoned off through excessive allowances, fuel expenses, and travel costs.

a6166.speaker: Edward Chileka Banda, CEO of NGORA
a6166.speech: Said, during the launch of the localisation debate in Lilongwe, that NGOs in Malawi are spending a disproportionate amount of the funds they mobilize on non-essential costs, leaving only a fraction for the communities they claim to serve: “There is a culture where NGOs spend more money on allowances, travel, and fuel than on actual projects that benefit the poor. In some cases, 90% of the mobilized funds are spent on these overhead costs, and a paltry 10% is what trickles down to the community” ; “For example, people are traveling to Mulanje spending K10 million on allowances while only K500,000 goes to support the community. This doesn’t make sense. This is the kind of resource capture that must stop” ; “We cannot talk about development if this culture of allowances continues. We must change the way NGOs operate to ensure that more money reaches the people who need it.”

a6166.speaker: Edward Chileka Banda, CEO of NGORA
a6166.speech: Argued that persistent poverty is a direct result of a system that prioritizes lavish allowances and travel expenses for NGO staff over tangible aid for the poor; stressed that the localisation agenda is the perfect opportunity to reassess and realign the way NGOs operate in Malawi and noted that a systemic overhaul is necessary to ensure that foreign aid and NGO resources are used effectively and responsibly.

a6166.speaker: Bernadetta Mkonyola, representing the UN Resident Coordinator in Malawi
a6166.speech: Highlighted the importance of localization, emphasising that empowering local communities, particularly women, youth, and the elderly, is the key to driving true development: “Localization is not just about trickling down money; it’s about giving power to communities to sit at the table with decision-makers” ; “Only through consultation with those on the ground can we ensure that development agendas are relevant and sustainable.”

a6194.speaker: James Gatwech Jok, Nasir County Commissioner
a6194.speech: “We are in peace and we are okay. Even the whole Payams around Nasir.” ; “The challenge now is the food inside the town because… the World Food Programme dropped food in some areas of the Payam, but inside the town, there is no food drop coming.” ; “We requested a lot about the river. Food that was meant to be brought by boat has not yet come. This is the only challenge. The rest is okay. We have no problem.”

a6194.speaker: James Gatwech Jok, Nasir County Commissioner
a6194.speech: Said the improved security situation had encouraged many displaced residents to return, particularly from neighboring Ethiopia and other parts of South Sudan; added that while food airdrops have been made to remote areas, Nasir town — now hosting the largest share of returnees — has not received any recent deliveries, either by air or via the Sobat River.

a6194.speaker: James Gatwech Jok, Nasir County Commissioner
a6194.speech: Is appealing to the World Food Programme (WFP) and other humanitarian partners to urgently scale up support for the returnees, including food, shelter materials, and medical assistance.

a6279.speaker: Alain Foka, journalist
a6279.speech: In his column published on his YouTube channel Alain Foka Officiel on Tuesday 11 March 2025, reacted to the humiliation suffered by Ukraine in the United States, considering that this situation confirms the correctness of the decision by the countries of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) — Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger — to end their military cooperation with the United States and France; for him this episode illustrates a reality: international aid always comes with strings attached, often unfavourable to the recipient countries.

a6279.speaker: Alain Foka, journalist
a6279.speech: Declared that Africans must draw lessons from the Ukrainian experience; stressed that African leaders must always keep in mind that the interest of their country must be their absolute priority; recalled that the promises of the great powers are nothing but words and that fine speeches often conceal carefully calculated interests: “The grand speeches about aid are nothing but lures to be wary of. Leaders must be fully aware of this. These sales pitches always conceal a sober design. There is no friendship between States, there are only interests. All those who invite you to go to war and to fight this or that neighbour, who offer to intervene militarily in your country, do so for interests that are their own. There is no reason why they would do it simply for your beautiful eyes, when they too have their own problems at home. Expressions of the sort ‘our African friends’, the falsely friendly pats on the shoulder, too often conceal well-packaged swindles. Some of our leaders have paid the price for having listened to the leaders of great powers who promised them the moon. At the end of the day, they found themselves utterly destitute and quite alone. One must have the courage to take responsibility when you are right and when the options proposed to you from outside are not in line with your interests. It is in this that the leaders of the AES showed extraordinary merit in putting an end to this fruitless, budget-devouring and humiliating military aid which, for more than 10 years, resolved nothing.”

a6300.speaker: Ismail Omar Guelleh, President of Djibouti
a6300.speech: Has always raised the questions of governance, social justice, stability and security; he has proclaimed loud and clear that it was essential to tackle the real ills that prevent the durability of peace agreements in Africa ; in his speech on Tuesday he presented the evolution of the very concept of mediation, proposing to move "from a firefighter's approach to that of an architect."

a6300.speaker: UNHCR (HCR)
a6300.speech: According to UNHCR, the civil war that broke out in 2013 has caused more than 300,000 deaths, displaced nearly 2 million people inside the country and created 2.5 million refugees in neighbouring countries.

a6300.speaker: Latest reports from AMISOM and the AU Peace and Security Council
a6300.speech: According to these reports, the central government "is not yet in a position to assume this responsibility" for security.

a6300.speaker: Joint UN-AU report presented last May
a6300.speech: Highlighted the resurgence of Shabaab attacks, which shelled with mortars the United Nations headquarters itself in Mogadishu and carried out in March two major attacks in the capital by detonating no fewer than 28 bombs.

a6300.speaker: 10th High-Level Retreat of the African Union Commission
a6300.speech: Concluded that Africa must succeed in all its programmes, without exception, and begin without delay by deeply reforming the security sector, promoting justice and good governance and ensuring perfect stability in order to achieve real and substantial development.

a6340.speaker: Kamudoni Nyasulu, Senior Counsel, prosecutor, certified fraud examiner and consultant on governance reforms
a6340.speech: Has highlighted gaps in the implementation of public finance management reforms and proposed time-bound outcomes to reap from programmes such as the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) ; observed, in an analysis covering 2013 to 2025, that the Malawi Government made repeated commitments to strengthen law enforcement and prosecutorial institutions, particularly in response to corruption scandals and governance failures, but with minimal action.

a6340.speaker: Kamudoni Nyasulu, Senior Counsel, prosecutor, certified fraud examiner and consultant on governance reforms
a6340.speech: Observed that following the revelations of Cashgate an IMF Country Report No. 14/37 documented Malawi's commitment to prosecuting perpetrators, conducting forensic audits and strengthening Ifmis controls ; said: “While arrests and prosecutions occurred, many cases were delayed or lacked transparency. Despite some high-profile prosecutions, asset recovery remained fragmented and ineffective. The forensic audit, though completed, was not fully leveraged to secure convictions. Public sector reforms were initiated, but progressed slowly, undermining donor confidence and leading to aid suspensions.”

a6340.speaker: Kamudoni Nyasulu, Senior Counsel, prosecutor, certified fraud examiner and consultant on governance reforms
a6340.speech: Noted that during the same period, Capital Hill, in its reports to the IMF, consistently pledged to strengthen internal and external audit systems, enhance Integrated Financial Management and Information System (Ifmis) oversight and implement forensic audits; said that while the commitment rhetoric remained strong, the repetition of similar pledges year after year signalled institutional inertia and reform fatigue, which undermines credibility and donor confidence ; said: “Routine audits repeatedly failed to detect systemic fraud. Internal audit units lacked independence and resources; external audits were delayed and poorly enforced. These gaps created a permissive environment for financial abuse, including the later Covid-19 funds mismanagement. Forensic audits were commissioned post – Cashgate and occasionally post-disbursement, but never institutionalised. Reports show limited capacity, delayed investigations, and weak prosecutorial follow-through.”

a6340.speaker: Kamudoni Nyasulu, Senior Counsel, prosecutor, certified fraud examiner and consultant on governance reforms
a6340.speech: Called for embedding prosecutorial independence within legal frameworks, enhancing inter-agency coordination, and leveraging donor conditionality, saying these are critical steps toward building a resilient and transparent justice system.

a6340.speaker: IMF Country Report No. 14/37
a6340.speech: Documented Malawi's commitment to prosecuting perpetrators, conducting forensic audits and strengthening Ifmis controls.

a6340.speaker: Christopher Mbukwa, Mzuzu University-based economist
a6340.speech: Said in a written response yesterday that recurrence of promises without actions puts Malawi in a bad light. He said: “It signals weak political will and an ill-equipped public administration to deliver on Malawi's political commitments in the area of strengthening public finance management.”

a6340.speaker: Joseph Mwanamvekha, Minister of Finance, Economic Planning and Development
a6340.speech: Did not respond to our questions yesterday.

a6340.speaker: Joseph Mwanamvekha, Minister of Finance, Economic Planning and Development
