a6340.speech: Is quoted as having assured the IMF delegation, at a meeting with IMF Africa Department director Abebe Selassie on the sidelines of the IMF and World Bank Group Annual Meetings in Washington, of Malawi's strong political will and reaffirmed that President Peter Mutharika, who triumphed in the September 16 2025 General Election, has already started fiscal measures to strengthen economic stability.

a6348.speaker: Federation for National Peace & Development (PEFENAP)
a6348.speech: Has called on the Malawi government to prioritize the safety and welfare of its citizens caught in the escalating conflict between Israel and Iran.

a6348.speaker: Edwards Chaka, PEFENAP Executive Director
a6348.speech: Said in an exclusive interview with Malawi24 that while it is the responsibility of the Israeli government to implement local safety measures, Malawi must take proactive steps to protect its nationals in both Israel and Iran. “Our primary concern is the safety and well-being of our citizens not only in Israel but also those in Iran. While it remains the responsibility of the Israeli government to guide safety measures, the Malawi government should take immediate action to guarantee their protection, including evacuation if necessary,” Chaka said. He further urged the Malawian authorities to work closely with Israeli and Iranian officials to guarantee that there is a clear and reliable communication channel with its nationals in the two countries and make sure that Malawian nationals receive equal protection and assistance as local citizens.

a6348.speaker: Edwards Chaka, PEFENAP Executive Director
a6348.speech: Warned that the Israel-Iran war risks spiralling into a broader global conflict, which could pose severe challenges for developing countries like Malawi, particularly through economic instability, food insecurity, and reduced foreign aid. He then emphasized the need for urgent government action and regional diplomatic engagement to shield Malawi from the ripple effects. “Israel and Iran's war may ignite a global conflict that may pose significant risks to developing countries like Malawi, primarily through disruptions to supply chains, increased food insecurity, and economic instability,” he cautioned.

a6348.speaker: Edwards Chaka, PEFENAP Executive Director
a6348.speech: On food security, Chaka said that Malawi's heavy reliance on agriculture makes it particularly vulnerable to disruptions in the supply of critical inputs like fertiliser. He cited the Ukraine war's impact on fertiliser availability as an example of how distant conflicts can hit close to home.

a6434.speaker: Abdirahman Abdishakur, Somali opposition MP
a6434.speech: Reminded people that China once had Africa's largest embassy in Mogadishu in the 1960s, but today the lack of interest is clear: "But who is to blame? Is it on our side?"

a6434.speaker: Jibril Qoobey, social media commentator
a6434.speech: Argues that China's aid is minimal compared to Western support: "USAID alone gave over $150 million in aid to Somalis. Compare that to $28 million. It is nothing. All in all, there is no comparison between the West's support and the Chinese."

a6434.speaker: Ali Mohamud, journalist
a6434.speech: Raised concerns about China's lending practices, warning that Chinese loans often result in African countries losing control of key infrastructure when debts cannot be repaid: "That is exactly what China is doing to many African countries. It is like ransom—where you indebt someone and wait until they become broke."

a6545.speaker: Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, head of Sudan’s Sovereign Council
a6545.speech: In March of this year, demanded that Chad stop cooperating with the United Arab Emirates and close the Amdjarass base.

a6545.speaker: United Arab Emirates
a6545.speech: Continued to send weapons, describing them as humanitarian aid, already using N’Djamena airport instead of Amdjarass.

a6545.speaker: Le Monde (newspaper)
a6545.speech: According to Le Monde, the UAE continued to send weapons, describing them as humanitarian aid, using N’Djamena airport instead of Amdjarass.

a6545.speaker: Abdoulaye-Sabre Fadoul, Chadian Minister of State
a6545.speech: Spoke during a panel at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum on the theme “Rethinking Global Cooperation against Terrorism”, in which he stressed the complexity of the fight against terrorism and called for efforts to be united.

a6545.speaker: Turkish sources (anonymous)
a6545.speech: According to Turkish sources, al-Burhan’s invitation to the forum was part of the Turkish government’s plan to normalise relations between Chad and Sudan and to restore relations between Deby and the head of Sudan’s sovereign council.

a6720.speaker: Study/presentation ‘Bridging Faith and Health to Address Stigma and Support HIV Prevention Towards 95-95-95 Goals’ (USAID Kizazi Hodari project)
a6720.speech: Spotlighted the role of faith leaders in promoting awareness and reducing stigma.

a6720.speaker: Dr Mussa Ndile, Monitoring, Evaluation Research and Learning Director for the USAID Kizazi Hodari Northeastern Zone project
a6720.speech: Noted that through training and advocacy, over 57,700 individuals were reached and hundreds were linked to critical HIV services ; said the faith leaders also mobilised resources to support treatment adherence for orphaned and vulnerable children and their caregivers.

a6720.speaker: Study “Deploying Multi-Method Interventions Towards Sustaining Paediatric HVL Suppression in Mara”
a6720.speech: Focused on tailored interventions for children with high viral loads; found that strategies such as ART adherence calendars, psychosocial counselling and family-based support achieved a 93 per cent viral load suppression rate, demonstrating the effectiveness of combining clinical and community care.

a6720.speaker: Presentation “Tracing Back to Care After Interruption in Treatment”
a6720.speech: Told the story of a 14-year-old boy in Tanga who, with help from a community worker and enhanced adherence counselling, returned to care after treatment interruption and achieved viral load suppression, showcasing the power of community support in overcoming barriers to care.

a6778.speaker: Lagos State Ambulance Services (LASAMBUS)
a6778.speech: Has raised concerns over impersonators and vandals hindering rescue operations, even as it reported an impressive 97.5 percent emergency response rate over the past four years, responding to 44,152 out of 45,277 calls received between 2021 and 2025.

a6778.speaker: Kemi Ogunyemi, Special Adviser to the Lagos State Governor on Health
a6778.speech: Disclosed the 97.5% response rate following a review of LASAMBUS operations and performance reports and described the achievement as evidence of the service's dedication to providing swift and professional emergency medical response across the State; said 36,919 patients were treated during the review period, with 11,200 of them in 2023 alone, that LASAMBUS recorded zero in-transit deaths in 2022 and 2025 due to robust triage systems, prompt stabilization and the professionalism of its paramedics, and reported a 100% survival rate of patients transported in 2025 compared to 60% in 2021, describing it as a reflection of improved pre-hospital care in Lagos State.

a6778.speaker: Kemi Ogunyemi, Special Adviser to the Lagos State Governor on Health
a6778.speech: Noted that urgent public support is needed to sustain and improve LASAMBUS's life-saving operations and expressed concern over challenges affecting its operations, including impersonation, vandalism of assets, assault on personnel, and lack of public cooperation in traffic situations; appealed to residents to give ambulances the right of way and refrain from obstructing emergency operations at accident scenes: "Every second counts in an emergency. Obstructions can cost lives."

a6778.speaker: Kemi Ogunyemi, Special Adviser to the Lagos State Governor on Health
a6778.speech: Warned against fraudulent individuals posing as LASAMBUS officials and advised the public to only dial 767 or 112 for authentic emergency ambulance services; condemned the rising incidents of ambulance vandalism and attacks on emergency personnel, describing such acts as criminal and dangerous to patients depending on urgent medical intervention.

a6778.speaker: Kemi Ogunyemi, Special Adviser to the Lagos State Governor on Health
a6778.speech: Noted that a total of 931 field assignments were executed by LASAMBUS in the past four years, with 350 of them completed in 2024 alone, attributing this to increased public health campaigns and readiness drills, and announced that a proposal to upgrade LASAMBUS from a department to a full-fledged agency is currently being reviewed by Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu to enhance operational autonomy and coordination.

a6778.speaker: Kemi Ogunyemi, Special Adviser to the Lagos State Governor on Health
a6778.speech: Explained that LASAMBUS has grown from a modest unit with 21 staff and four station wagons in 2001 to a robust emergency system with 36 Mobile ICUs, three Mobile Clinics and five Transport Ambulances, operating from four major bases and 26 ambulance points across Lagos; disclosed that LASAMBUS now has 196 personnel, including 64 Nurses, 74 Community Health Extension Workers (CHEWs), 70 trained ambulance pilots and support staff, all certified in Basic Life Support and First Aid, with 75% certified in Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support.

a6778.speaker: Kemi Ogunyemi, Special Adviser to the Lagos State Governor on Health
a6778.speech: Highlighted recent renovations at ambulance bases in LASUTH, General Hospital Lagos, General Hospital Ikorodu and General Hospital Badagry, the construction of a new base at Eti-Osa MCC by the State Government, and the upgrading of five ambulance points at the Old Lagos-Ibadan Toll Gate, Eti-Osa, Anthony, Third Mainland Bridge and Mile 12 funded by the Saving One Million Lives Programme for Results (SOML-PforR); commended LASAMBUS workers as unsung heroes who risk their lives to save others and urged Lagosians to support and protect them.

a6820.speaker: George Nkhoma, chairperson of Golden Dairy Cooperative (retired soldier)
a6820.speech: “We asked ourselves this question and realised it was possible to use the local resources as a starting point. The pasture here is abundant.” ; “We decided we had the land, the resources and the determination. All we needed was to come together and take the first step.” ; “We were comfortable growing maize, beans and groundnuts. But when we saw the growth of dairy farming elsewhere, we realised we were missing something bigger.”

a6820.speaker: George Nkhoma, chairperson of Golden Dairy Cooperative
a6820.speech: “So far, we have fulfilled half of our required contribution and received K41.8 million from Agcom, which we have used to purchase 50 head of cattle for 50 of our 100 members.”

a6820.speaker: George Nkhoma, chairperson of Golden Dairy Cooperative
a6820.speech: “We are learning more about how to care for the cows. We are getting better at feeding them, managing their health and ensuring they are well looked after.”

a6820.speaker: George Nkhoma, chairperson of Golden Dairy Cooperative
a6820.speech: “We are part of something bigger. Dairy farming has brought new opportunities and new hope to our community.”

a6820.speaker: Feranji Thunga, member of Golden Dairy Cooperative
a6820.speech: “We knew that if we didn’t come together, it would never happen. Alone, we couldn’t make it work.” ; “We didn’t have much to start with,” … “But we knew we had to contribute something. Each of us gave what we could.”

a6820.speaker: Feranji Thunga, member of Golden Dairy Cooperative
a6820.speech: “We are using it [the manure] to improve our crops and the results are clear. Our maize fields are healthier and the bananas are thriving like never before.”

a6820.speaker: Feranji Thunga, member of Golden Dairy Cooperative
a6820.speech: “With the cows, the crops and the training we have received, I know my children will have a better life. I will be able to educate them without worrying about how to pay school fees. I will give them opportunities I never had.” ; “I will expand my crop production, grow more maize, bananas and other vegetables and use the income to send my children to school.” ; “One day, I will build a modern house for my family. A house we can be proud of, with enough space for my children to study and grow. And most importantly, we will never go hungry again. The farm will provide everything we need. I can see it so clearly in my mind and it feels so real now.”

a6820.speaker: Michael Kumpoto, member of Golden Dairy Cooperative
a6820.speech: “We had heard of many projects before but not all of them came to fruition. The idea of giving away our money and resources—without knowing for sure that we would get the support we needed—felt risky.”

a6820.speaker: Michael Kumpoto, member of Golden Dairy Cooperative
a6820.speech: Is confident that this success will inspire neighbouring farmers to venture into dairy farming themselves: “When people see the benefits that we are reaping, they will want to join us. The cows have already made such a difference in our lives.”

a6820.speaker: Christopher Nkhoma, member of Golden Dairy Cooperative
a6820.speech: “Before the cows arrived, we had to buy expensive fertilisers. But now, we use the manure from the cows and it works just as well, if not better. It is saving us money.”

a6820.speaker: Teddie Nakhumwa, Agcom National Coordinator
a6820.speech: Believes that the success of farmer groups receiving support from Agcom holds great promise for the future of agriculture in Malawi, and that when farmers embrace farming on such an advanced scale the possibility of revolutionising the country’s agricultural sector becomes not only attainable but increasingly realistic. Says that in Phase 2, Agcom has broadened its scope by including aggregators, processors, anchor farmers and exporters: “We believe this makes the commercial concept even more complete. We have learned valuable lessons from Agcom Phase 1, which focused largely on farmers and buyers.”

a6820.speaker: Teddie Nakhumwa, Agcom National Coordinator
a6820.speech: Acknowledges that there was initial reluctance and scepticism about the programme’s viability, with many farmers unsure about the level of support, but notes that over time Agcom’s approach has proven its worth and that more awareness campaigns and real success stories have resulted in an overwhelming response in Agcom Phase 2: “They now realise that with the right resources, training and support, they can contribute to revolutionising agriculture in Malawi.”

a6820.speaker: Teddie Nakhumwa, Agcom National Coordinator
a6820.speech: Believes that the success of Agcom Phase 1, which was funded by the World Bank to the tune of $95 million, has attracted more partners, including the Irish Government, the European Union and the Flemish Government, who have joined the World Bank in the $326 million Agcom Phase 2.

a6848.speaker: Marine Le Pen, president of the Rassemblement National group in the French National Assembly
a6848.speech: Criticises the CNDA's decision to grant the right of asylum to Palestinians from Gaza, denouncing an “unconditional reception” that she judges dangerous; reacted strongly to the decision of the National Court of Asylum Law (CNDA) to grant Palestinians from Gaza the possibility of applying for refugee status in France; in a speech relayed on social media, describes the measure as an “unconditional reception” and “pure madness”, arguing that it weakens French society through decisions she judges ideological and dangerous; says the reception of Palestinians risks importing tensions linked to the conflict, or even facilitating the entry of Hamas supporters.

a6848.speaker: Marine Le Pen, president of the Rassemblement National group in the French National Assembly
a6848.speech: Blames the inaction of the Gulf countries, which favour financial aid; questions the absence of solidarity of the Gulf countries, such as Saudi Arabia or the United Arab Emirates, which, despite their declared support for the Palestinian cause, do not take in these refugees on a large scale.

a6848.speaker: National Court of Asylum Law (CNDA), decision of 11 July 2025
a6848.speech: Rests on the recognition of the persecutions suffered by Palestinians in Gaza on account of their nationality, in a territory ravaged by the conflict between Israel and Hamas, granting Palestinians from Gaza the possibility of applying for refugee status in France.

a6848.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a6848.speech: According to the UN, more than 80% of Gaza's 2.3 million inhabitants depend on humanitarian aid.

a7256.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a7256.speech: “Mr Sotinrin’s proven ability to mobilise capital, innovate in agribusiness, and collaborate across sectors will be instrumental in repositioning the Bank of Agriculture as a catalyst for food security, sovereignty and rural prosperity,” President Tinubu emphasised.

a7256.speaker: Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to the President (Information & Strategy) (press statement)
a7256.speech: Announced that President Bola Tinubu has appointed Ayo Sotinrin as the new Managing Director of the Bank of Agriculture, effective immediately, and that the appointment aligns with the Tinubu administration's strategy to revitalise Nigeria's agricultural sector.

a7265.speaker: Obedi Opoko, younger brother of the late Susan Unyiyo
a7265.speech: Said his sister was attempting to mine gold in a bid to support her children, following a reduction in humanitarian assistance; in an exclusive interview with Eye Radio, confirmed that two sisters were involved in the incident. “They were actually hustling, looking for gold, and then the soil fell on them. Two of them. One passed away. This happened in Imvepi camp, near a church called Vranige. Yesterday, the body was brought to the church. She was around 35 years old,” he said.

a7265.speaker: Ugandan media reports
a7265.speech: Indicate that many refugees in the Imvepi settlement have resorted to informal gold digging along the Ore River using rudimentary tools and without safety equipment.

a7383.speaker: Purvance Heuer, managing director of Arysteq Asset Management
a7383.speech: "With the South African Rand consistently depreciating over the last 20 years, the Arysteq Global Opportunities Fund allows investors to diversify their investments and enjoy exposure to international currencies in some of the most innovative and well-established markets." ; Said the Arysteq Global Opportunities Fund aims to outperform the MSCI World Index to maximise long-term capital appreciation, achieved by investing in listed equities in developed markets globally, allowing investors to achieve a better risk-adjusted return. ; "Our investment philosophy, which is our 'DNA', gives us an edge. It is centred around four key principles, namely liquidity, quality, a margin of safety and a longer-term view."

a7408.speaker: SADC secretariat (statement on its X handle)
a7408.speech: Said AfDB director for regional integration coordination Dr Joy Kategekwa will deliver the public lecture, which will start at 1400 hours: “The public lecture offers a unique platform for engaging and promises to be an insightful forum for dialogue and knowledge exchange among leading think-tanks, policymakers, practitioners, non-state actors, development partners and the public, including the youth and influential voices driving Africa’s integration agenda.” ; said the lecture also offers an opportunity for networking with other stakeholders who are committed to realising the continent’s development aspirations.

a7408.speaker: SADC secretariat (statement on its X handle)
a7408.speech: Said Dr Kategekwa is a respected international trade and investment lawyer who has dedicated her career to structuring Africa’s trade policy, negotiations and industry landscape for sustainable development, and to ensure that Africa’s integration into global trade is beneficial and wealth creating ; said Dr Kategekwa is passionate about building the next generation of Africa’s trade law/policy practitioners and has spent over 15 years offering guest lectures on international trade, investment, regional integration and development at leading global centres of learning.

a7476.speaker: South Africa's Special Investigating Unit (SIU)
a7476.speech: Has filed a case at the Special Tribunal seeking to reclaim R390 million from Gumede over an allegedly fraudulent and inflated personal protective equipment contract awarded during the COVID-19 pandemic; alleges that Gumede manipulated procurement processes to secure this deal with the South African Police Service (SAPS), leading to an “unlawful overcharge” that cost taxpayers millions.

a7476.speaker: South Africa's Special Investigating Unit (SIU), affidavit
a7476.speech: Describes the funnelling of large sums through a network of companies linked to Gumede as a deliberate scheme to enrich individuals without delivering value to the government ; makes the damning assertion: “These respondents, through their insatiable greed, have directly or indirectly caused unnecessary deaths of frontline police officers and have certainly resulted in the theft of SAPS funds.”

a7476.speaker: Daily Maverick (investigative reporting)
a7476.speech: Investigative reporting cited as bolstering the SIU's case, outlining multiple irregularities in the contract: false promises of direct imports, local resale at inflated prices, failure to deliver full orders, and substandard products.

a7476.speaker: Robert Gumede, South African businessman (Guma Group)
a7476.speech: Assured authorities that the PPE would be imported via a specially chartered Airbus from China — an aircraft that never materialized.

a7476.speaker: Robert Gumede and Blessing Qwabe
a7476.speech: Despite having four months to formally respond, have instead attacked the case as “baseless” while avoiding sworn affidavits to counter the allegations ; Gumede dismisses these allegations as politically motivated.
